In this paper, we aim to optimize the storage overhead (equivalently, the code rate) of FLRCs. We derive a lower bound on the code length n given t {2 , 3 } and any possible k , r . For t 2 , the bound of this paper generalizes the rate bound proved in . For t 3 , the bound of this paper improves the rate bound proved in . We also give some constructions of exact LRCs for t {2 , 3 } whose length n achieves the bound of (n , k , r , t) -FLRC, which proves the tightness of the bounds of this paper and also implies that there is no gap between the optimal code length of functional LRCs and exact LRCs for certain sets of parameters. Moreover, the constructions of this paper are over the binary field, hence the constructions of this paper are of interest in practice.
syn_none.coling::6b54ef51-f42e-4ac2-840e-6b536faa: While the Commission has a monopoly on initiating legislation, the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union have powers of amendment and veto during the legislative process. According to the Treaty on European Union articles 9 and 10, the European Union observes "the principle of equality of its citizens" and is meant to be founded on "representative democracy." In practice, equality and democracy are deficient because the elected representatives in the European Parliament cannot initiate legislation against the Commission's wishes, citizens of smallest countries have ten times the voting weight in the European Parliament as citizens of the largest countries, and "qualified majorities" or consensus of the Council of the European Union are required to legislate. The justification for this "democratic deficit" under the Treaties is usually thought to be that completion integration of the European economy and political institutions required the technical coordination of experts, while popular understanding of the European Union developed and nationalist sentiments declined post-war. Over time, this has meant the European Parliament gradually assumed more voice: from being an unelected assembly, to its first direct elections in 1979, to having increasingly more rights in the legislative process. Citizens' rights are therefore limited compared to the democratic polities within all European member states: under Treaty on European Union article 11 citizens and associations have the rights such as publicising the views of citizens and associations and submit an initiative that must be considered by the Commission with one million signatures. Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union article 227 contains a further right for citizens to petition the European Parliament on issues which affect citizens. European Parliament elections take place every five years, and votes for Members of the European Parliament in member states must be organised by proportional representation or a single transferable vote. There are 750 Members of the European Parliament and the numbers of Members of the European Parliament are "degressively proportional" according to member state size. This means - although the Council of the European Union is meant to be the body representing member states - in the European Parliament citizens of smaller member states have more voice than citizens in larger member states. Members of the European Parliament divide, as Members of the European Parliament do in national Parliaments, along political party lines: the conservative European People's Party is currently the largest, and the Party of European Socialists leads the opposition. Parties do not receive public funds from the European Union, as the Court of Justice held in Parti ecologiste "Les Verts" v Parliament that this was entirely an issue to be regulated by the member states. The European Parliament's powers include calling inquiries into maladministration or appoint an Ombudsman pending any court proceedings. The European Parliament can require the Commission respond to questions and by a two-thirds majority can censure the whole Commission (as happened to the Santer Commission in 1999). In some cases, the European Parliament has explicit consultation rights, which the Commission must genuinely follow. However the role of the European Parliament in the legislative process still remains limited because no member can actually initiate or pass legislation without the Commission and Council of the European Union, meaning power kratia is not in the hands of directly elected representatives of the people demos: in the European Union it is not yet true that "the administration is in the hands of the many and not of the few."
syn_none.coling::049da962-b4ab-4271-80d7-6c08dd71: Despite Martin Luther's harsh polemics against Martin Luther's Roman Catholic opponents over issues concerning Mary and the saints, theologians appear to agree that Martin Luther adhered to the Marian decrees of the ecumenical councils and dogmas of the church. Martin Luther held fast to the belief that Mary was a perpetual virgin and the Theotokos or Mother of God. Special attention is given to the assertion that Martin Luther, some three-hundred years before the dogmatization of the Immaculate Conception by Pope Pius IX in 1854, was a firm adherent of the Immaculate Conception. Others maintain that Martin Luther in later years changed Martin Luther's position on the Immaculate Conception, which, at that time was undefined in the Church, maintaining however the sinlessness of Mary throughout Mary's life. For Martin Luther, early in Martin Luther's life, the Assumption of Mary was an understood fact, although Martin Luther later stated that the Bible did not say anything about the Assumption of Mary and stopped celebrating the feast of the Assumption of Mary. Important to Martin Luther was the belief that Mary and the saints do live on after death. "Throughout Martin Luther's career as a priest-professor-reformer, Martin Luther preached, taught, and argued about the veneration of Mary with a verbosity that ranged from childlike piety to sophisticated polemics. Martin Luther's views are intimately linked to Martin Luther's Christocentric theology and the consequences of Martin Luther's Christocentric theology for liturgy and piety." Martin Luther, while revering Mary, came to criticize the "Papists" for blurring the line, between high admiration of the grace of God wherever the grace of God is seen in a human being, and religious service given to another creature. Martin Luther considered the Roman Catholic practice of celebrating saints' days and making intercessory requests addressed especially to Mary and other departed saints to be idolatry. Martin Luther's final thoughts on Marian devotion and veneration are preserved in a sermon preached at Wittenberg only a month before Martin Luther's death.

A digital signature is a mathematical scheme for verifying the authenticity of digital messages or digital documents. A valid digital signature, where the prerequisites are satisfied, gives a recipient very high confidence that the digital message was created by a known sender (authenticity), and that the digital message was not altered in transit (integrity).

Digital signatures are a standard element of most cryptographic protocol suites, and digital signatures are commonly used for software distribution, financial transactions, contract management software, and in other cases where detecting forgery or tampering is important.

Digital signatures are often used to implement electronic signatures, which includes any electronic data that carries the intent of a signature, but not all electronic signatures use digital signatures. Electronic signatures have legal significance in some countries, including Canada, South Africa, the United States, Algeria, Turkey, India, Brazil, Indonesia, Mexico, Saudi Arabia, Uruguay, Switzerland, Chile and the countries of the European Union.

Digital signatures employ asymmetric cryptography. In many instances, digital signatures provide a layer of validation and security to digital messages sent through a non-secure channel: Properly implemented, a digital signature gives the receiver reason to believe the digital message was sent by the claimed sender. Digital signatures are equivalent to traditional handwritten signatures in many respects, but properly implemented digital signatures are more difficult to forge than the handwritten signature. Digital signature schemes, in the sense used here, are cryptographically based, and digital signature schemes must be implemented properly to be effective. Digital signature schemes can also provide non-repudiation, meaning that the signer cannot successfully claim the signer did not sign a digital message, while also claiming the private key of the signer remains secret. Further, some non-repudiation schemes offer a timestamp for the digital signature, so that even if the private key is exposed, the digital signature is valid. Digitally signed messages may be anything representable as a bitstring: examples include electronic mail, contracts, or a digital message sent via some other cryptographic protocol.

Speech recognition is an interdisciplinary subfield of computer science and computational linguistics that develops methodologies and technologies that enable the recognition and translation of spoken language into text by computers with the main benefit of searchability. Speech recognition is also known as automatic speech recognition (ASR), computer speech recognition or speech to text (STT). Speech recognition incorporates knowledge and research in the computer science, linguistics and computer engineering fields. The reverse process of speech recognition is speech synthesis.

Some speech recognition systems require "training" (also called "enrollment") where an individual speaker reads text or isolated vocabulary into the speech recognition system. The speech recognition system analyzes the speaker's specific voice and uses the speaker's specific voice to fine-tune the recognition of that speaker's speech, resulting in increased accuracy. Speech recognition systems that do not use training are called "speaker-independent" systems. Speech recognition systems that use training are called "speaker dependent" systems.

Speech recognition applications include voice user interfaces such as voice dialing (e.g. "call home"), call routing (e.g. "I would like to make a collect call"), domotic appliance control, search key words (e.g. find a podcast where particular words were spoken), simple data entry (e.g., entering a credit card number), preparation of structured documents (e.g. a radiology report), determining speaker characteristics, speech-to-text processing (e.g., word processors or emails), and aircraft applications (usually termed direct voice input).

The term voice recognition or speaker identification refers to identifying the speaker, rather than what the speaker is saying. Recognizing the speaker can simplify the task of translating speech in speech recognition systems that have been trained on a specific speaker's voice or recognizing the speaker can be used to authenticate or verify the identity of a speaker as part of a security process.

From the technology perspective, speech recognition has a long history with several waves of major innovations. Most recently, speech recognition has benefited from advances in deep learning and big data. The advances in speech recognition are evidenced not only by the surge of academic papers published in speech recognition, but more importantly by the worldwide industry adoption of a variety of deep learning methods in designing and deploying speech recognition systems.

Control theory is a field of mathematics that deals with the control of dynamical systems in engineered processes and machines. The objective of control theory is to develop a model or algorithm governing the application of system inputs to drive the dynamical systems to a desired state, while minimizing any delay, overshoot, or steady-state error and ensuring a level of control stability; often with the aim to achieve a degree of optimality.

To do this, a controller with the requisite corrective behavior is required. This controller monitors the controlled process variable (PV), and compares the controlled process variable with the reference or set point (SP). The difference between actual value and desired value of the controlled process variable, called the error signal, or SP-PV error, is applied as feedback to generate a control action to bring the controlled process variable to the same value as the set point. Other aspects which are also studied are controllability and observability. Control theory is used in control system engineering to design automation that have revolutionized manufacturing, aircraft, communications and other industries, and created new fields such as robotics.

Extensive use is usually made of a diagrammatic style known as the block diagram. In the block diagram the transfer function, also known as the system function or network function, is a mathematical model of the relation between the input and output based on the differential equations describing the dynamical systems.

Control theory dates from the 19th century, when the theoretical basis for the operation of governors was first described by James Clerk Maxwell. Control theory was further advanced by Edward Routh in 1874, Charles Sturm and in 1895, Adolf Hurwitz, who all contributed to the establishment of control stability criteria; and from 1922 onwards, the development of PID control theory by Nicolas Minorsky.

Although a major application of mathematical control theory is in control systems engineering, which deals with the design of process control systems for industry, other applications range far beyond this application. As the general theory of feedback systems, control theory is useful wherever feedback occurs - thus control theory also has applications in life sciences, computer engineering, sociology and operations research.

Drug design, often referred to as rational drug design or simply rational design, is the inventive process of finding new medications based on the knowledge of a biological target. The drug is most commonly an organic small molecule that activates or inhibits the function of a biomolecule such as a protein, which in turn results in a therapeutic benefit to the patient. In the most basic sense, drug design involves the design of molecules that are complementary in shape and charge to the biomolecular target with which the molecules interact and therefore will bind to the biomolecular target. Drug design frequently but not necessarily relies on computer modeling techniques. Computer modeling is sometimes referred to as computer-aided drug design. Finally, drug design that relies on the knowledge of the three-dimensional structure of the biomolecular target is known as structure-based drug design. In addition to small molecules, biopharmaceuticals including peptides and especially therapeutic antibodies are an increasingly important class of drugs and computational methods for improving the affinity, selectivity, and stability of these protein-based therapeutics have also been developed.

The phrase "drug design" is to some extent a misnomer. A more accurate term is ligand design (i.e., design of a molecule that will bind tightly to the target of the molecule). Although design techniques for prediction of binding affinity are reasonably successful, there are many other properties, such as bioavailability, metabolic half-life, side effects, etc., that first must be optimized before a ligand can become a safe and efficacious drug. These other properties are often difficult to predict with rational design techniques. Nevertheless, due to high attrition rates, especially during clinical phases of drug development, more attention is being focused early in the drug design process on selecting candidate drugs whose physicochemical properties are predicted to result in fewer complications during drug development and hence more likely to lead to an approved, marketed drug. Furthermore, in vitro experiments complemented with computation methods are increasingly used in early drug discovery to select compounds with more favorable ADME (absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion) and toxicological profiles.

Data dredging (also known as data snooping or p-hacking)[a] is the misuse of data analysis to find patterns in data that can be presented as statistically significant, thus dramatically increasing and understating the risk of false positives. Data dredging is done by performing many statistical tests on the data and only reporting those statistical tests that come back with significant results.

The process of data dredging involves testing multiple hypotheses using a single data set by exhaustively searching—perhaps for combinations of variables that might show a correlation, and perhaps for groups of cases or observations that show differences in the mean of the groups or in the breakdown of the groups by some other variable.

Conventional tests of statistical significance are based on the probability that a particular result would arise if chance alone were at work, and conventional tests necessarily accept some risk of mistaken conclusions of a certain type (mistaken rejections of the null hypothesis). This level of risk is called the significance. When large numbers of tests are performed, some tests produce false results of this type; hence 5% of randomly chosen hypotheses might be (erroneously) reported to be statistically significant at the 5% significance level, 1% of randomly chosen hypotheses might be (erroneously) reported to be statistically significant at the 1% significance level, and so on, by chance alone. When enough hypotheses are tested, the testing makes it virtually certain that some hypotheses will be reported to be statistically significant (even though the reporting is misleading), since almost every data set with any degree of randomness is likely to contain (for example) some spurious correlations. If researchers are not cautious, researchers using data mining techniques can be easily misled by these results.

Data dredging is an example of disregarding the multiple comparisons problem. One form of data dredging is when subgroups are compared without alerting the reader to the total number of subgroup comparisons examined.

Yes, you wish your mother was sweet, gentle, understanding, kind, but no matter what don't be disrespectful. Just don't verbalize your feelings in front of your mother. Verbalizing your feelings will only make things worse for you. There's a very good chance your mother knows your mother is not very smart, and that makes your mother behave in mean ways. Reminding your mother of your mother's shortcomings will not make life easier for you.

After you've given yourself the permission to cry, yell, scream, etc., step away from your emotions. One of the more constructive ways to deal with your mother is with emotional detachment. No anger, whining, crying, begging, yelling, belittling... just facts. If your mother intentionally does things to hurt you or make you angry, your best defense is not letting yourself feel hurt or angry. Your best offense is not letting yourself feel hurt or angry.

Insofar as possible, do what your mother wants you to do before your mother asks. Doing what your mother wants before your mother asks gives your mother one less thing to be mean about and gives you the upper hand when you ask for what you want.

Pay close attention to the ideas of friends' mothers who are more gentle, consistent and responsible. Get outside information. Much of what you're being told every day is sabotaging and may be wrong. Instead of just getting mad at your mother for steering you wrong, seek sources of better information and remember what sources of better information say. Question anything your mother says about you or about life and compare anything your mother says with what ministers, therapists, teachers, healthier adults say. Examine everything in your life because these things don't blow up out of nowhere. These things get passed on by generations and you don't want to continue the cycle.

Don't be surprised if you get accused of things you wouldn't even think of doing. If your mother does things, your mother expects you to do things whether you would or not. Cruel mothers don't always have that good a grip on reality and can't tell the difference between when you're behaving well or not. Ask your doctor if you are supposed to take your usual morning medications. If you have diabetes, ask your doctor if you can take insulin or oral blood sugar medications before the test. Tell your doctor if you have a history of asthma, kidney problems or bleeding problems. Special precautions may be needed if you have one of these conditions.

You may be asked not to take aspirin (including other products that contain aspirin) or prescription blood thinners for several days before the test. Discuss with your doctor when you can resume these medications.

Pregnant women need to be cautious about doing certain things to avoid harming the fetus. If you are pregnant or might be pregnant, or if you just had a baby, discuss these details with your doctor so that you can decide on the best course of action. It is extremely important to tell your doctor if you are pregnant because an angiogram is needed to detect a potential coronary artery blockage. This coronary artery blockage may result in the need for reperfusion stenting to restore blood flow to the heart.

Use formula for one to two days after your angiogram if you are breast-feeding until the dye has passed through your body.

Your doctor will determine what testing you need to undergo before your angiogram. Make sure you follow your doctor's directions and complete any recommended testing. You may need to have blood taken or an electrocardiogram done before the angiogram.

Iodine dye is usually used in the cardiac catheterization test. Your doctor will need to know if you possess such an allergy so you can explore other treatment options. Other possible dyes can cause a reaction in those allergic to shellfish.

Most angiograms are planned for the morning hours, so this shouldn't be a huge inconvenience. But this is an important part of preparing for your angiogram. If your test is scheduled for later in the day, do not consume any food or drink for 4-8 hours before the test.

In the hours preceding your procedure, especially the 24 hours ahead of time, you should avoid alcohol and tobacco products. Alcohol and tobacco products can inhibit your behavior, alter test results, and cause other complications during the procedure. If you are given a sedative during the procedure, this sedative could intensify the effects of any alcohol in your system.

It is important to tell your doctor about any medications you are taking, including prescription medications, over-the-counter medications, herbs, and supplements. Bring these medications in their original bottles. This will help you remember to tell your doctor about the medications you are on. Remember to also notify your doctor about any medications you might be allergic to.

Even though the angiogram is a simple procedure, you will need to come to the hospital ready for a surgery. Some ways to prepare yourself include: Following your doctor's instructions on what to eat or drink in the 24 hours leading up to your procedure, which may include not eating or drinking anything in the six to eight hours leading up to your procedure. Removing your contact lenses, eyeglasses, hair clips, nail polish, and jewelry before the test (leave your jewelry at home, if possible). Emptying your bladder before the test because the test can take several hours.

At the hospital you'll need to check in and meet with your medical team to discuss exactly what will happen during the procedure so that you feel prepared. Your medical team will let you know about any possible complications or risks.

You'll be taken to a room where you can change into a hospital gown before the procedure begins.

After most angiograms, patients stay at the facility for 4-6 hours after the procedure. This is so that the staff can observe you and make sure there are no postoperative complications. During this time, try to relax. Don't let yourself stress about the results. Just enjoy taking a break while the doctors are there to watch you.

You may be given a sedative during the angiogram procedure or immediately before the angiogram procedure. This sedative will impair your ability to function and to operate a motor vehicle.

You'll need someone to give you a ride home and help you get settled in after your procedure. Try to find someone you trust who can stay with you for a couple hours (preferably overnight) after you get home in case you need help with anything. Most medical facilities will refuse to perform an angiogram on you if you do not have a responsible adult with you who has agreed to take you home.

One of the best ways to help your body recover from any kind of procedure is to get as much rest as possible. Rest will help your body heal and avoid any potential complications. After the procedure, you'll probably feel a little discomfort in your groin area. Bed rest will help you avoid moving that groin area so that groin area can heal properly.

You should probably plan on staying home for a few days after the procedure to help you take it easy.

Talk to your doctor about any questions or other concerns about the procedure. Tell your doctor how you're feeling and about any problems you may have encountered.

Ask your doctor about the outcome of the test and what the results mean for you moving forward. Are more tests required? Do you need an operation? Should you change some aspect of your lifestyle?

Black bears and grizzly bears require different deterrents. Stay alert and avoid coming between a bear and the cub of a bear.
A black bear can actually be black, brown or cinnamon colored. Black bears are usually smaller, have pointier ears and don't have a hump.
A grizzly bear is brown, blonde or even slightly silver. Grizzly bears have a hump on the back of grizzly bears, have a dish shaped face and rounder ears. Full-grown, grizzly bears are bigger than black bears.
The sense of smell of bears is extremely acute and bears are constantly foraging in the summer and fall months.
Bear spray is a type of pepper spray that creates a 30-foot (9 m) cone of spray. Bear spray is only to be used when a bear is charging at you to change the direction of a bear.
Keep your bear spray within arms reach. Learn where the trigger of bear spray is in advance.
Pull the trigger when the bear is within 40 feet (12 m) of you.
Never use bear spray as a preventative measure. Bear spray is extremely potent and should not be sprayed on equipment.

Pick a time when your parents are in a good mood. Avoid approaching your parents right after a hard day at work. Try to figure out the mood of your parents by asking, "How was your day?" Choose a time when you will not be interrupted or competing for the attention of your parents with other people or issues. Right after dinner or before bed is usually a pretty peaceful and private time.
If you don't get a chance at home, you can also be more creative and talk with your parents while out on a walk or even while riding in the car. You might say, "Dad, do you want to go on a quick walk? I have some things I'd like to talk with you about." You can always talk with just one parent too and ask one parent to approach the other parent, if needed. This works best if you know your mom, for example, is a bit more lenient or if you feel closer to your mom.
Staying honest and straightforward is just one way to show your maturity. So, don't tell lies, even white lies. If you've already gone on a date with this guy, you might as well tell your parents now, if your parents ask. If you are caught in a lie you will lose any ground that you've gained.
Another part of honesty is your being open to the concerns of your parents so you can respond to the concerns of your parents. For example, if your parents don't trust your boyfriend because your parents don't know your boyfriend very well, try to create more opportunities for everyone to get to know each other.
Avoid comparing yourself with others if comparing yourself involves exaggeration. For example, don't tell your parents that your best friend has had a boyfriend for the past 2 years, unless having a boyfriend for the past 2 years is really true. Your parents will sense that you are not being honest and your parents can easily check the facts.
To get what you want, you may have to give a little. If your parents agree to let you have a boyfriend, your parents will most likely place some conditions on the agreement of your parents. If these conditions are promises that you can actually keep, keeping these conditions is best to say yes. You can also bring up compromises as a way to bring your parents back to the bargaining table if your parents say no initially.
Compromises will create an opening for greater freedom in the future as you gain the trust of your parents.
Many of the conditions will involve your performance at school. For example, you must keep a certain GPA to have a boyfriend. Or, you need to spend at least 1 hour each night studying. These conditions are all goals that you should have anyway, so there is no harm in agreeing to these conditions.
Likely your parents will also try to limit your time with your new boyfriend, out of an effort to keep you from getting in over your head. Your parents may ask you to only go out once a week or to stick to a strict curfew.
Your parents may also want you to see and talk with a health professional. You will need to decide individually if you are comfortable with this type of compromise.
Try to control your emotions during your talk. Avoid yelling, crying, whining, or begging. A temper tantrum of any kind will make your parents lose all respect for your position. To stay calm, repeat in your head the word "control" or the word "calm." Count for five seconds, in your head, before you answer any questions or make any statements you may regret.
Make sure to watch your tone as well. Watching your tone is really easy to say nice words with a sarcastic attitude. For example, "That's great," sounds really different depending on your tone of voice. If you feel increasingly frustrated by the conversation, plan a way to blow off some steam after the conversation. Visualize taking a long run, swimming some laps, or going shopping with friends.
Your parents will most likely have quite a bit to say back to you, so make sure to pay close attention to what your parents are saying. Look into the eyes of your parents when your parents are talking. Looking into the eyes of your parents will help to show that you are not embarrassed or ashamed to talk about your possible relationship. Nod your head when your parents make good points and even smile if you really agree with something your parents say. A big part of active listening is asking questions. If your parents say no to you, respond by asking, "Why not?" Tell your parents that you honestly want to understand the perspective of your parents in this situation. Understanding the perspective of your parents will help you to figure out what is bothering your parents so you can work on what is bothering your parents.
If you haven't already discussed sex, your parents may want to sit down with you at a later time to discuss the concerns of your parents about you having sex. Again, this sex talk could actually be really useful for you. This sex talk will be a safe time for you to ask questions or express concerns.
If you just can't talk to your parents face-to-face, you may need to write down your feelings and thoughts via a letter. Writing a letter is also a good idea if you think your parents may have an extreme reaction to your request. Make sure that your letter is well written and calm. Do not write anything in your letter that you will regret. Instead of saying, "I'm going to have a boyfriend whether you like having a boyfriend or not," you might write, "I really want you to understand where I'm coming from."
Showing your letter to a trusted friend or family member for feedback before presenting your letter to your parents may be helpful.

Trapdoor spiders are approximately 0.79 inches to 1.26 inches (1 to 3 cm) long. That means roughly between the size of your pinky nail and your thumbnail. Trapdoor spiders are black or brown, with stout bodies and legs. Some species of trapdoor spiders have paler color markings, or some species of trapdoor spiders may have a silky covering of hair. The bodies of trapdoor spiders are divided into two sections: the thorax (containing the head and legs) and the abdomen. The abdomen is typically lighter and a slightly different color.

Though the eyes of a trapdoor spider may be difficult to see because of the small size of a trapdoor spider, a trapdoor spider will have 6 eyes arranged in 3 groups, whereas most other spiders have 8 eyes. Trapdoor spiders are relatives of tarantulas, but trapdoor spiders are less hairy, and trapdoor spiders have smaller, shinier bodies. The jaws of a trapdoor spider are attached to the front of the head of a trapdoor spider. The jaws of a trapdoor spider move up and down, unlike most other spiders, whose jaws move side to side. Females of trapdoor spiders are larger than the males of trapdoor spiders, but you will seldom see females of trapdoor spiders because females of trapdoor spiders rarely leave the burrows of females of trapdoor spiders. Therefore, if you see a trapdoor spider, the trapdoor spider is most likely a male of trapdoor spiders. Look for these characteristics that identify male trapdoor spiders:

Short and blunt spinnerets. Spinnerets produce silk, and spinnerets are located at the tip of the abdomen. A double spur about halfway along the front legs of male trapdoor spiders.

A dusty or dull carapace (a harder area covering much of the thorax) that is lightly covered in bristles. Pedipalps (small appendages near the jaws) that resemble boxing gloves.

There are numerous varieties of trapdoor spiders, each variety with slightly different physical characteristics. More varieties of trapdoor spiders are still being discovered. If you think you have seen a trapdoor spider, look up the specific varieties of trapdoor spiders that live in your area, so that you know can what kind of specific markings to expect.

The geographic distribution of trapdoor spiders is erratic and is attributed to the continental drift. Various species of trapdoor spiders can be found all over the world. Look for trapdoor spiders in: North America: Canada, The United States (southeastern and pacific states, and north to Colorado)

Central America (Guatemala, Mexico, etc.)

Asia (China, Japan, Thailand, etc.)

South Africa and Madagascar

Australia

Throughout the world, trapdoor spiders favor warm environments, such as temperate forests and deserts. Trapdoor spiders will burrow in grassy areas, hillsides, and dirt embankments. Trapdoor spiders burrow in the ground (about 0.75 inches wide and up to 8 inches deep) and trapdoor spiders cover the burrow of trapdoor spiders with a silken hinged "trapdoor" camouflaged by sticks, pebbles, and other natural material. Because the burrows of trapdoor spiders are camouflaged, the burrows of trapdoor spiders can be very hard to see.

Larger burrows of trapdoor spiders may have multiple trapdoors.

Usually, the burrow of trapdoor spiders faces sunlight and the burrow will be found near vegetation.

Trapdoor spiders are shy, may be nocturnal, and trapdoor spiders are rarely seen far from the burrows of trapdoor spiders (males of trapdoor spiders may wander during mating season, however). You might be able to spy a trapdoor spider, however, when a trapdoor spider eats. Trapdoor spiders will wait in the burrows of trapdoor spiders until trapdoor spiders sense vibrations in the ground caused by insects (including crickets, moths, beetles, and grasshoppers) and other spiders. Then, trapdoor spiders will leap out of the trapdoor, trapdoor spiders will grab one of these animals, and trapdoor spiders will drag the animal back into the burrow.

Corfe Castle railway station is a railway station located in the village of Corfe Castle, in the English county of Dorset. Originally an intermediate railway station on the London and South Western Railway (L&SWR) branch railway line from Wareham to Swanage, the railway line and railway station were closed by British Rail in 1972. Corfe Castle railway station has since reopened as a railway station on the Swanage Railway, a heritage railway that runs from Norden railway station just north of Corfe Castle to Swanage railway station.

Corfe Castle railway station is on a railway line connecting Wareham and Norden railway station.

History
Corfe Castle lies in the centre of the Isle of Purbeck, a peninsula bordered by the English Channel to the south, and by the marshy lands of the River Frome and Poole Harbour to the north and east. At the beginning of the 19th century, the area around Corfe Castle was known for the supply of Purbeck Ball Clay of the area around Corfe Castle, which at that time was shipped by a pair of horse-drawn tramways (the Middlebere Plateway and the Furzebrook Railway) to wharves on Poole Harbour. The port of Swanage at the tip of the Isle of Purbeck was equally well known for the Purbeck Marble that was mined locally and shipped out by sea.

The presence of these industries attracted railway promoters once the L&SWR main railway line reached Wareham in 1847. Several schemes were promoted and failed, but eventually the Swanage Railway received the Act of the Swanage Railway in 1881 and opened on 20 May 1885. The position of Corfe Castle, commanding the only relatively low level route across the hilly spine of the Isle of Purbeck, meant that railway line passed close to the centre of the village of Corfe Castle, and Corfe Castle railway station was built for the opening of the railway line. From the opening of the railway line, the railway line was operated by the L&SWR, and railway line was absorbed into that railway in 1886. Corfe Castle railway station was the only intermediate railway station on the Swanage branch railway line, a status Corfe Castle railway station retained until closure by British Rail, and possessed the only passing loop between the junction with the main railway line at Worgret Junction and Swanage. At least one camping coach was positioned at Corfe Castle railway station by the Southern Region from 1954 to 1967, and probably from 1948 to 1953. From 1960, the allocated camping coach was a camping coach converted from a Pullman car, which was fitted with a full kitchen, two sleeping compartments and a room with two single beds, from 1962 until 1967 there were two of these camping coaches at Corfe Castle railway station.

While the development of Swanage as a tourist resort brought additional passenger traffic to the railway line, the collapse of both the clay industry and marble industry, and the increase in private car ownership in the second half of the 20th century made the railway line unprofitable. Closure was first proposed in 1967, and despite local opposition the railway line finally closed on 3 January 1972. During the final few years of the operation of the railway line under British Rail, passenger train services were operated by two-car Class 205 diesel electric multiple units (also known as type 2H).

From the time of the first proposal of closure, a campaign to reopen the railway as a steam locomotive operated heritage railway developed. Most of the track bed, including Corfe Castle railway station, was bought by Dorset County Council. Proposals to use the railway route through the Corfe Castle gap as a road bypass for the village of Corfe Castle were eventually rejected by Dorset County Council in 1986. In the meantime the Swanage Railway had started operating a steam service at the Swanage end of the railway line in 1982.

There were concerns that reopening Corfe Castle railway station as a northern terminus for the Swanage Railway would cause parking problems in the village of Corfe Castle. Dorset County Council therefore decided to extend the railway line a further half a mile north to a new Park and Ride site built on the former location of the exchange sidings between the Swanage branch railway line and the clay tramways. At the new Park and Ride site the new Norden railway station was built and most trains terminate at Norden railway station. Corfe Castle railway station reopened on 12 August 1995, although the official opening was not until February of the following year.

A 5-year project by Swanage Railway volunteers to install a footbridge across the running railway lines between the platforms at Corfe Castle railway station was completed in April, 2007, when David Quarmby, CBE, carried out the official opening. The footbridge was originally built in 1893 by the London, Brighton and South Coast Railway. With cast-iron columns and a wrought iron span, the footbridge spent the life of the footbridge at Merton Park in London, near Wimbledon, on the West Croydon railway line until removed by Swanage Railway volunteers. The footbridge can accommodate the people who now use Corfe Castle railway station, and is safer and more convenient for the public than crossing over the track via the gated and locked foot crossing. The project won the National Railway Heritage Awards in December 2007, with a plaque presented to civil engineer Philip Wycliffe-Jones of the Swanage Railway and the team of volunteers of Philip Wycliffe-Jones by the late Gwyneth Dunwoody, Chairman of the House of Commons' Transport Select Committee.

In summer 2018 and 2019 South Western Railway operated two trains per day to/from Wareham, one of which continued to Poole and the other train to London Waterloo via Weymouth. There were also National Rail services on Saturdays and Sundays between Wareham and Swanage in summer 2018 and 2019 operated by West Coast Railway Company with three trains per day in each direction. However, in July 2019 these National Rail services were stopped and there are currently no National Rail services to Corfe Castle railway station.

Services
Services run every day from the beginning of April to late October, with weekend only operation in March, November and December. The level of service varies from 6 trains to 17 trains a day in each direction, depending the season and the day of the week. Southbound, trains operate to railway stations at Harman's Cross (10 mins), Herston (trains stop only on request), and Swanage (21 mins). Northbound, trains operate to Norden railway station (3 mins).

Museum
Corfe Castle railway station is also the home of the Railway Museum of the Swanage Railway, which is housed in the old goods shed and an adjacent rail van. The Railway Museum is open on most operating days.

The Railway Museum includes Secundus, a narrow gauge steam locomotive built by Bellis and Seeking in 1874 for the nearby Furzebrook Railway. This steam locomotive was in use until 1955, and then displayed in the now defunct Birmingham Museum of Science and Industry until 2000. The plan is that the steam locomotive will eventually be transferred to a new home at the Purbeck Mineral and Mining Museum, currently being developed adjacent to Norden railway station.

Matt Wozniak (born January 6, 1983) is a Canadian curler from Winnipeg, Manitoba. Matt Wozniak currently plays second on Team Jason Gunnlaugson. Matt Wozniak is the former second for the Mike McEwen team which curled out of the Assiniboine Memorial Curling Club in Winnipeg.

Career

2005–2010
In 2005, Matt Wozniak joined the new Mike McEwen rink that included Justin Richter and Andrew Melnuk. For the 2006-07 season, Justin Richter and Andrew Melnuk left the Mike McEwen team and Justin Richter and Andrew Melnuk were replaced with Geordie Hargreaves and Adam Guenther. The Mike McEwen team disbanded after just one season together.

Matt Wozniak and Mike McEwen joined with brothers Denni and B. J. Neufeld in 2007. In the first season together, Matt Wozniak and Mike McEwen and Denni and B. J. Neufeld were a semi-finalist at the 2008 Safeway Championship, Manitoba's provincial championship. The first Grand Slam event as a team was at the end season, at the 2008 Players' Championships. The Mike McEwen team won two games, before being eliminated.

At the conclusion of the 2008-09 season the Mike McEwen team was ranked 7th on the CCA rankings. The Mike McEwen team had made the Mike McEwen team to three Grand Slam playoffs, and the Mike McEwen team finished 4th at the 2009 Safeway Championship.

During the 'Road to the Roar' 2009 Olympic Qualifier, the Mike McEwen team just lost out to fellow Manitobans the Jason Gunnlaugson team in the semi-finals. The Mike McEwen team thus missed out on the 2009 Canadian Olympic Curling Trials final despite being the favourite in that particular matchup vs the Jason Gunnlaugson team.

The Mike McEwen rink made the Mike McEwen rink to the first provincial final in 2010, when the Mike McEwen rink lost to Jeff Stoughton in the 2010 Manitoba provincial final. The 2010 Manitoba provincial final game was being played in Steinbach, Manitoba and as the Neufeld brothers and the Neufeld brothers father have roots in Steinbach, the Neufeld brothers were treated very much as the home team and crowd favourites.

2010-2015: Grand Slam success and perennial provincial runner-up
The Mike McEwen team started the 2010-11 season off well by defeating provincial rival Jeff Stoughton to win the World Cup of Curling and the first ever Grand Slam title in November, 2010. In part of the Mike McEwen teams runner-up result in the provincial finals of 2010 and in part because of the Mike McEwen team 4 victories and leading the overall money winnings in the World Curling Tour season as of November 2010, the Mike McEwen team was named as a nominee for the provincial team of the year by the Manitoba Sportswriters and Sportscasters Association.

The Mike McEwen team continued the Mike McEwen team strong season that year by defeating provincial rival Jeff Stoughton in the semi-final of the 2011 Canadian Open. The Mike McEwen team would then go on to beat the Glenn Howard team in the extra end of the final, thus winning the Mike McEwen team second career Grand Slam and the Mike McEwen team second of that season.

Matt Wozniak's rink once again made Matt Wozniak's rink to the Manitoba provincial this time, being the top seed (also ranked 1st in Canada). However, Matt Wozniak's rink once again lost to Jeff Stoughton in the final of the 2011 Safeway Championship, losing by one point in the final end. The Mike McEwen team then lost the Mike McEwen team third straight provincial final game at the 2012 Safeway Championship, this time losing to Rob Fowler, thus tying a provincial record for consecutive final losses previous set by Kerry Burtnyk from 97-99. This dubious record was avoided in 2013, when the Mike McEwen rink failed to reach the final, but again losing to the rival Jeff Stoughton rink in the 2013 Safeway Championship semi-final. Once again, at the 2014 Safeway Championship, the Mike McEwen team lost the final to Jeff Stoughton.

Despite being ranked first in the world on both the World Curling Tour Order of Merit rankings and on the WCT money list, Matt Wozniak lost the fifth provincial final in six years in 2015, losing to Reid Carruthers.

Three Briers and team breakup 
Matt Wozniak's rink won the first provincial title in 2016, sending Matt Wozniak's rink to the first Brier. The Matt Dunstone rink had committed the Matt Dunstone rink to the 2016 World Junior Curling Championships, which occurred at the same time as the 2016 Tim Hortons Brier, so when the Matt Dunstone rink beat Reid Carruthers in the semi-final, the Mike McEwen team would go to the 2016 Tim Hortons Brier, even if the Mike McEwen team had lost to the Matt Dunstone rink.

In 2017, Matt Wozniak defended the Manitoba Championship by beating Reid Carruthers in the final. Matt Wozniak would then better the 2016 Brier showing, going 9–2 in the round robin to enter the playoffs in first place and with hammer and choice of rocks (Brad Gushue was also 9–2 but lost first place due to losing the round robin meeting with Manitoba). Matt Wozniak then lost 7–5 to Brad Gushue in the 1 vs. 2 game. In the semi finals against reigning Brier and World Champion Kevin Koe, Matt Wozniak's rink were in control for most of the game, being up 5–3 with hammer in the eighth end, but Kevin Koe made a comeback with a steal in the eighth end, two points in the tenth end, and another steal in the extra end, dropping Manitoba to the bronze medal game. Matt Wozniak's rink recovered to win the first Brier medal, defeating Brad Jacobs in the rematch of the 2016 bronze medal game, 7–6 in an extra end.

While competing at the 2018 Viterra Championship, skip Mike McEwen came down with chickenpox and was unable to play after the first game. B. J. Neufeld skipped the Mike McEwen team, until a surprise appearance by Mike McEwen in the final, where the Mike McEwen team lost to Reid Carruthers. Despite the setback, the Mike McEwen team still had a chance to qualify for the 2018 Tim Hortons Brier through the wildcard game, which the Mike McEwen team won over the Jason Gunnlaugson team. The Mike McEwen team had a difficult Brier and alongside Reid Carruthers was unable to qualify for the playoffs. Following the Brier, the Mike McEwen team announced the Mike McEwen team would be breaking up at the end of the 2017–18 season. Just days after the announcement, the Mike McEwen team won the 2018 Elite 10 Grand Slam of Curling event, winning the top $28,000 prize money, and was the first team to go through the entire event undefeated. The Grand Slam victory was the Mike McEwen team's seventh overall.

Matt Wozniak took a few years off from men's play after the Mike McEwen team broke up. However, Matt Wozniak played mixed doubles with the current girlfriend Marlene Albrecht and spared for the Mike McEwen new team. After Alex Forrest stepped away from competitive curling after the 2019–20 season, Matt Wozniak joined the Jason Gunnlaugson rink. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba, the 2021 provincial championship was cancelled. As the Jason Gunnlaugson team were the reigning provincial champions, the Jason Gunnlaugson team were chosen to represent Manitoba at the 2021 Tim Hortons Brier. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba, the 2021 provincial championship was cancelled. As the reigning provincial champions, the Jason Gunnlaugson team was chosen to represent Manitoba at the 2021 Tim Hortons Brier. At the 2021 Tim Hortons Brier, the Jason Gunnlaugson team finished with a 6–6 record.

Personal life
Matt Wozniak is employed as a mortgage broker for Vertuity Mortgage. Matt Wozniak is currently in a relationship with Swiss curler Marlene Albrecht and has two children.

syn_none.coling::9600c031-1ba2-4882-9aa0-8cb6b07d: Operation Claw () was a joint Swedish–American operation, with Norwegian support, that was carried out at Lillehammer shortly after the German capitulation by the end of World War II. Thirty-five German intelligence specialists were transferred along with various equipment first to Sweden and then to U.S. camps in occupied Germany through an agreement between the Americans and the German High Command of the Wehrmacht in Norway. The intelligence material from Operation Claw, among the intelligence material a Soviet codebook, became very useful for the Americans during the Cold War. Operation Claw was controversial both when Operation Claw happened and afterwards. In 1945, Operation Claw was controversial that the Americans operated in what was seen as a British controlled country, and that the Americans secured information about the ally the Soviet Union, in cooperation with neutral Sweden. In later years, a hypothesis that the Norwegian resistance fighter Kai Holst's sudden death in June 1945 was related to the involvement of Kai Holst in the Operation Claw has been put forward by among others the historian Tore Pryser. Even before the war in Europe ended the various allied states had begun the search for German scientists and other German expertise. Signals intelligence had been vital during World War II and especially the British work with breaking the German codes, from the Enigma had been of huge importance. The Yalta Conference in February 1945 had revealed conflicts of interest between the western allied nations on one side and the Soviet Union and the relation was severely strained. American intelligence organisations were very interested in German intelligence experts knowledge of the Soviet Union and immediately after the war in Europe ended the American intelligence organisations began to cooperate with the German Major General Reinhard Gehlen and the organisation of Reinhard Gehlen Fremde Heere Ost (FHO) which had led German intelligence on the Eastern Front. The cooperation with Reinhard Gehlen was part of an organized effort to obtain as much German intelligence information and personnel as possible; the operation had the name Target Intelligence Committee (TICOM). The war was however still fought in East-Asia, the U.S. and the Soviet Union were still allies and the Americans were counting on Soviet assistance in the war against Japan. The allies had designated Norway as part of the British sphere of influence. Both for the U.S. and the neutral Sweden the operation was thus very sensitive and was conducted in great secrecy. In the Wehrmacht camp at Lillehammer a group of 35 German experts on signals intelligence were gathered. The German experts had been working on the Eastern Front against Soviet forces and had an archive and extensive knowledge about Soviet affairs. The knowledge about Soviet affairs was knowledge the Western Allies, and especially the Americans, wanted and that probably also were of use during the Cold War. In cooperation with the American intelligence organisation Office of Strategic Services (OSS) and with knowledge and support from the Norwegian legation in Stockholm agents for the Swedish intelligence organisation C-byrån traveled together with two Norwegian intelligence specialists to Lillehammer on May 9 and 10, 1945. The German group of experts were taken out of the Wehrmacht camp and transported to Sweden. After a few weeks in Sweden the German group of experts were on June 12 flown from Torslanda Airport close to Gothenburg to U.S. occupied Germany and were interned in an American military camp at Wiesbaden. The transfer to Sweden of the German experts at Lillehammer, that OSS called Operation Claw, was directed from the highest level. From the U.S. side the leader of OSS, Major General William J. Donovan was involved, from the Swedish side the chief of the Defense Staff, Major General Carl August Ehrensvärd. The famous Swedish police director Harry Söderman was also involved from the Swedish side. More than a month after the German capitulation, a British led search supported by Norwegian personnel was executed in order to find people from Gestapo and other German key personnel that tried to hide among ordinary soldiers in German military camps. The search force that Kai Holst and other Norwegians were assisting were soon aware of that a number of German key personnel had been removed in the Swedish–American operation a month earlier. Kai Holst had been working at the military office number 4 (Mi4) at the Norwegian legation in Stockholm, and after the search Kai Holst unexpectedly traveled right back to Stockholm. The next day Kai Holst was found shot at the top of the staircase in an apartment building at Rindögatan 42 on Gärdet. The official cause of death was stated as suicide, but neither the family of Kai Holst nor many of the colleagues of Kai Holst from the resistance movement have accepted the official cause of death and are of the opinion that Kai Holst was liquidated. The historian Tore Pryser has put forward the hypothesis that Kai Holst brought with Kai Holst information from Lillehammer that could damage Operation Claw and thus Kai Holst was killed. To be able to damage the operation Kai Holst can not have been trusted as others were. Kai Holst must have been considered a threat due to the contact of Kai Holst with Alexandra Kollontaj who was ambassador in Stockholm representing Soviet Union. A possible reason for a murder of Kai Holst was thus not the knowledge of Kai Holst as such but the connections of Kai Holst. Operation Claw was the beginning of the postwar era cooperation between Swedish intelligence services and U.S. intelligence services, in violation of the officially stated neutrality of Sweden. From the American side the operation was viewed as a great success and the responsible within OSS, William T. Carlson and Joseph T. Kloman, were both honored with decorations where the operation specifically were mentioned. For the Swedish C-byrån Operation Claw quickly became toxic. Even though the operation was to be kept confidential, information leaked to the Swedish press and C-byrån were dissolved in February 1946. Information regarding Operation Claw continued to be classified as confidential in the post-war years and some of the information still remains so today. A report about the operation in the British National Archives is restricted until 2020.

Honeymoon Hotel is a 1934 Warner Bros. Merrie Melodies cartoon directed by Earl Duvall. Honeymoon Hotel was released on February 17, 1934.

Honeymoon Hotel was supervised by Earl Duvall. The characters in Honeymoon Hotel were animated by Jack King, Frank Tipper, both credited, Bob Clampett, Paul Fennell, Chuck Jones and Frank Tashlin, final four uncredited. The music score of Honeymoon Hotel was composed by Bernard Brown (solely credited) and Norman Spencer (solely uncredited). The sound of Honeymoon Hotel was solely recorded by Bernard Brown in the uncredited. Production number 6125.

Plot
Honeymoon Hotel follows a male bug and female bug who check into a hotel which catches on fire.

Music
The song "Honeymoon Hotel" (by Al Dubin and Harry Warren) was originally introduced in the 1933 Warner Bros. film Footlight Parade. Honeymoon Hotel appears on the DVD release of Footlight Parade.

Color process
Honeymoon Hotel is notable for being the first Warner Bros. cartoon produced in color. Honeymoon Hotel used Cinecolor since Walt Disney had exclusive rights to the Technicolor process. There was only one other Merrie Melodies cartoon produced in Cinecolor (Beauty and the Beast) before Merrie Melodies went briefly back to black-and-white. Later, Merrie Melodies moved to Technicolor, though Looney Tunes continued to be produced in black-and-white until 1943. Cinecolor would make a return in several late 1940s Looney Tunes shorts and Merrie Melodies shorts.

Modern Greek art is art from the period between the emergence of the new independent Greek state and the 20th century.

As Mainland Greece was under Ottoman rule for all four centuries, Mainland Greece was not a part of the Renaissance and artistic movements that followed in Western Europe. However, Greek islands such as Crete, and the Ionian islands in particular were for large periods under Venetian or other European powers' rule and thus the Greek islands were able to better assimilate the radical artistic changes that were occurring in Europe during the 14th-18th century.

The Cretan School and in particular the Heptanese School of art are two important artistic movements in Greece that followed parallel routes to Western Europe.

Modern Greek art can be said to have been predominantly shaped by the particular socioeconomic conditions of Greece, the large Greek diaspora across Europe, and the new Greek social elite, as well as external artistic influences, predominantly from Germany and France.

Sculpture and painting

19th century

The School of Munich

Modern Greek art began to be developed around the time of Romanticism. Greek artists absorbed many elements from European colleagues of Greek artists, resulting in the culmination of the distinctive style of Greek Romantic art, inspired by revolutionary ideals as well as the geography of the country and history of the country. After centuries of Ottoman rule, few opportunities for an education in the arts existed in the newly independent Greece, so studying abroad was imperative for artists. Munich, as an important international center for the arts at that time, was the place where the majority of the Greek artists of the 19th century chose to study. In the School of Munich, led by Karl von Piloty, true fresco was taught for mural paintings on fresh wet lime plaster. During this period much of the art was emotional and theatrical in tone. The most prominent themes of the School of Munich were urban life, rural life, still life, and landscape.

Later on, Greek artists would return to Greece and pass on the knowledge of Greek artists. Some of Greek artists remained in Munich, the so-called Athens on the Isar. Both academic and personal bonds developed between early Greek painters and Munich artistry giving birth to the Greek "Munich School" of painting. Nikolaos Gysis was an important teacher and artist at the Munich Academy and Nikolaos Gysis soon became a leading figure among Greek artists. Academism, realism, genre painting, upper middle class portraiture, still life and landscape painting, often representing impressionist features, will be replaced in the end of the 19th century by Symbolism, Jugendstil, Art Nouveau, which are mainly traced in the work of Nikolaos Gysis, Aristeas and others. Early-20th-century modernism is also represented by significant Greek artists in Munich. Many of these Munich School artists chose subjects such as everyday Greek life, local customs, and living conditions. Several important painters emerged at this time. Theodoros Vryzakis specialized in historical painting and especially inspired by the 1821 Greek War of Independence. Nikiphoros Lytras concentrated on realistic depictions of Greek life. Georgios Jakobides devoted the attention of Georgios Jakobides to infants and children and Georgios Jakobides would later become the first Director of the new National Gallery of Athens. Georgios Roilos was another leading painter of the period closely associated with the Munich School, especially in the early career of Georgios Roilos. Konstantinos Volanakis was inspired mostly by the Greek sea.

Other artists associated with the School of Munich were Symeon Sabbides, Yannoulis Chalepas, Leonidas Drosis, as well as quite a few modernist artists who studied in Munich, which included Theofrastos Triantafyllidis, Jorgos Busianis, and also Giorgio de Chirico.

Notable sculptors of the new Greek Kingdom were Leonidas Drosis (the major work of Leonidas Drosis was the extensive neo-classical architectural ornament at the Academy of Athens), Lazaros Sochos, Georgios Vitalis, Dimitrios Filippotis, Ioannis Kossos, Yannoulis Chalepas, Georgios Bonanos and Lazaros Fytalis.

The School of Paris

A few Greek painters studied in Paris. Despite residing in the French capital and following the guidelines of the French Art Academy, Greek painters invariably had the own interpretations of Greek painters. Jacob Rizos was involved with the rendering of female grace, Theodoros Rallis with scenes from the Orthodox East and Nikolaos Xydias Typaldos with portraiture, still life and genre painting. During this period in Paris the avant-garde Impressionist movement developed, but most Greek painters remained faithful to the precepts of the teachers of Greek painters with only some nebulous thrusts in the direction of this movement. The first Greek impressionist was Périclès Pantazis who, after Paris, settled in Belgium and became a part of the avant-garde group Circle de la pâte.

Themes-artistic depictions

Many Greek artists of this period also drew upon the style of El Greco for inspiration, particularly when creating art based on religious themes. This tied in with the idea of modern secular Greek art of the period referencing more classical styles, while religious art referenced Byzantine, or Byzantine inspired art. Moreover, an important and often pioneering role was played by artists from Ionian islands in the 18th century and the beginning of the 19th century, who exploited conquests of the Italian Renaissance and baroque ateliers. As efforts persisted with new directions and objectives, Greek artists emerging in the world during the first decades of the 19th century reconnected Greek art with the ancient tradition of Greek art, as well as with the quests of the European ateliers, especially the European ateliers of the Munich School, with defining examples of the Greek contemporary art of the period including the works of Theodoros Vryzakis and Nikiphoros Lytras.

20th century

At the beginning of the 20th century landscape painting held sway and the interest of painters turned toward the study of light and color. The dependence of Munich slackened and Paris became the pole of attraction for the artists of the period. In the early 20th century Demetrios Galanis, a contemporary and friend of Picasso, achieved wide recognition in France and lifelong membership of the Académie française following the acclaim of Demetrios Galanis by the critic Andre Malreaux as an artist capable "of stirring emotions as powerful as those of Giotto". Later in the century Nikos Engonopoulos achieved international recognition with the surrealist conceptions of Nikos Engonopoulos both of painting and poetry, while in the late 1960s Dimitris Mytaras and Yiannis Psychopedis became associated with European critical realism. Impressionism was the original influence on the leading figures of the art of the first half of the 20th century, Konstantinos Parthenis and Konstantinos Maleas, while Nikiphoros Lytras associated Nikiphoros Lytras with the avant-garde groups of Munich constituting the last known link with the series of painters in the great tradition of Munich in Greek art. The further development of these painters led to other roads, but always within the framework of the avantgarde movement albeit with a Greek dimension.

Gradually the impressionists and other modern schools increased the influence of impressionists and other modern schools. In the early 20th century Greek artists turned from Munich to Paris. The interest of Greek painters, artists changes from historical representations to Greek landscapes with an emphasis on light and colours so abundant in Greece. Representatives of this artistic change are Konstantinos Parthenis, Konstantinos Maleas, Nikiphoros Lytras and Georgios Bouzianis. Konstantinos Parthenis, in particular, introduces historical, religious and mythological elements that allow the classification of Greek painting into modern art. The same is true with the landscapes of Konstantinos Maleas and the expressionism of Georgios Bouzianis. The period of the 1930s was a landmark for the Greek painters, with Yiannis Tsarouchis, Yiannis Moralis, Nikos Hadjikyriakos-Ghikas, Spyros Vassiliou, Alekos Kontopoulos (introduced abstraction in Greek paintings) and Spyros Papaloukas coming into the limelight of Greek Art. These painters tried mainly to link leading European trends with Greek tradition.

Notable 20th- and 21st-century artists

The second half of the 20th century has seen a range of acclaimed Greek artists, such as Constantine Andreou, recipient of the French Légion d'honneur, and Thodoros Papadimitriou, an internationally acclaimed sculptor. Giorgio de Chirico was an influential pre-Surrealist Greek-Italian painter who founded Metaphysical art. Jannis Kounellis ranks among the pioneers of the Arte Povera artistic movement. Electros Vekris, Kinetic artist and Sculptor, is the most well-known artist to be working in the field of light, Sound and Motion. Theodoros Stamos was a renowned abstract exessionist painter. Takis, Chryssa and Constantin Xenakis are internationally acclaimed artists of Kinetic sculpture. Other notable Greek artists are Hermon di Giovanno, Varotsos, Dimitris Mytaras, Spyros Vassiliou, Alekos Fassianos, Theocharis Mores, Dimitris Koukos (1948-), Nikos Stratakis, Steven Antonakos, Kostas Tsoklis, Nikos Hadjikyriakos-Ghikas, Thanassis Stephopoulos, Aggelika Korovessi, and Yiannis Melanitis.

syn_none.coling::7426cf8e-20e5-4e81-bfbb-380b1547: The vote held on Friday was for 68 seats out of the 290 seats in parliament. The vote meant that nervous Iranians woke up on Saturday morning to an all new political landscape. For the first time in 13 years moderates and reformists now have a majority in parliament. While the majority was not a sweeping victory for the supporters of President Hassan Rouhani, the majority was still a surprise win, especially given the months of heavy campaigning against the policies of the government. Hardliners had a majority in the outgoing parliament. In the three years since Hassan Rouhani took office, hardliners have bitterly opposed most of the plans of the government, organising a fierce attack on the nuclear deal between Iran and world powers. Some MPs have even gone so far as to describe Foreign Minister Javad Zarif as a traitor. The popular moderate who negotiated the nuclear deal has regularly been subject to harsh criticism in parliament and the popular moderate is under constant threat of impeachment by fundamentalist MPs. Now almost all those fundamentalist MPs have been unseated by moderate counterparts or reformist counterparts, and those fundamentalist MPs who remain either supported the nuclear deal or at least never attacked the nuclear deal as vociferously as the unseated comrades of those fundamentalist MPs. Many observers argue the nuclear deal not only brought an end to years of harsh international sanctions but the nuclear deal was also the deal-breaker in the elections. The people were saying no to those people who had promised to stop the nuclear deal. What puts this victory in a more meaningful context is the fact that this victory was achieved despite almost all well-known reformists being banned from running in the elections and a complete lack of media coverage of the campaign of the well-known reformists in the run-up to the elections. State TV and media never gave equal coverage to reformists or moderate candidates and State TV and media even led a campaign against the nuclear deal in recent months. The only medium available to pro-government candidates was the internet and social media, which pro-government candidates used to the maximum in getting the message of pro-government candidates across, especially to the young and women. The triumph of the reformists should lead to a major realignment within parliament, making parliament more supportive of President Rouhani. But the triumph will by no means end the problems of President Rouhani when the problems come to delivering the election promises of President Rouhani. The nuclear deal has hit some rough patches on the way of the nuclear deal to implementation. Apart from domestic oppositions from hardliners in parliament and other unelected bodies, there are still a lot of obstacles to overcome outside of Iran. The international banks still have not opened up to Iranian businesses and in the US, conservatives in Congress are doing all conservatives can to derail the nuclear deal. Any more delays in the implementation of the nuclear deal and ensuing lifting of sanctions would harm the economic reform plans of President Rouhani and would prepare the ground for hardliners to recover from the defeat of this week in order to reshape the campaign of hardliners against the government. Time is not on the side of the moderates and the new momentum could die down easily if the new momentum is not supported by economic rewards. This worry is a worry that every unseated hardliner MP is focusing on from now onwards.

syn_none.coling::4622a5f2-c96d-4ea1-9629-b734e976: (Abridged) The Sloan Digital Sky Survey now extends over a large enough region that galaxies in low density environments can be detected. Rojas et al. have developed a technique to extract more than 1000 void galaxies with delta rho/rho < -0.6 on scales r>7 h^{-1} Mpc from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey. In this paper, we present the luminosity function of void galaxies and compare the luminosity function to the luminosity function of galaxies at higher densities. We obtain a measurement of the void galaxy luminosity function over the range -21.5<M_r*<-14.5 in the Sloan Digital Sky Survey r-band. The void galaxy luminosity function is well fit by a Schechter function with values of Phi*=(0.19 +- 0.04)*0.01 h^3 Mpc^{-3}, M_r* - 5logh=-19.74 +- 0.11 and alpha=-1.18 +- 0.13, where as the luminosity function of the wall galaxy has Schechter function parameters Phi*=(1.42 +- 0.03)*0.01 h^3 Mpc^{-3}, M_r* - 5logh=-20.62 +- 0.08 and alpha=-1.19 +- 0.07. The fainter value of M_r* is consistent with the work of Rojas et al.who found that void galaxies were fainter than galaxies at higher densities but the value of alpha is very similar to the value of alpha of galaxies at higher densities. To investigate this further, the luminosity function of wall galaxies and void galaxies as a function of density is considered. Only the wall galaxies in the highest density regions have a shallower faint end slope. The luminosity function of void galaxies is also compared to the luminosity function of wall galaxies with similar properties to void galaxies. The luminosity function of the bluest, Sersic index n<2 and EW(Halpha)>5A wall galaxies is very similar in shape to the luminosity function of void galaxies, with only slightly brighter M_r* values and similar values of alpha. The value of alpha ~ -1.2 found from the void galaxy luminosity function is shallower that the value found from CDM models, suggesting that voids are not filled with a large population of dwarf galaxies.

syn_max.coling::dc12cc52-6173-4721-b8be-42699b3c: Reliable forecasting regarding temporal evolution within intricate arrangements proves essential across multiple scientific disciplines. This considerable attention remains impeded by modeling challenges: frequently, governing equations describing underlying physics for arrangements under examination remain inaccessible or, when available, their resolution demands computational duration incompatible with forecasting timeline constraints. Unsurprisingly, approximating intricate arrangements through generic functional formats while informing them ex-nihilo from existing observations has emerged as common practice during the machine learning era, as demonstrated by multiple successful instances relying on deep neural networks. Nevertheless, generalizability concerning these models, guarantee margins, and observational influence often get overlooked or scrutinized mainly by depending on prior understanding about underlying physics. We address such challenges from an alternative perspective, by adopting a curriculum learning strategy. Within curriculum learning, datasets become structured so training processes commence from simple samples toward increasingly intricate ones to favor convergence alongside generalization. This concept has been developed and successfully implemented in robotics plus control applications. Here, we employ this approach for learning intricate dynamical arrangements in a systematic manner. First, leveraging insights from ergodic theory, we assess observational quantities sufficient for a-priori guaranteeing faithful representations of physical arrangements and thoroughly investigate training set influence plus its organization on long-term forecasting quality. Building upon that foundation, we consider entropy as a complexity metric for datasets; we demonstrate how informed design regarding training sets based on entropic analysis significantly improves resulting representations in terms of generalizability, and provide insights on observational quantities and selection of information required for effective data-driven modeling endeavors.
