The CII 158 micron transition represents the dominant coolant of interstellar
matter in galaxies but substantial variations are seen from object to object.
The main source of radiation at a galactic scale remains poorly understood.
Previous studies of this emission in galaxies have a resolution of several
kpc or more so the observed signal is an average of different ISM components.
The aim of our work is to study, for the first time, CII radiation at the
scale of a spiral arm. We want to investigate the origin of such lines and their
use as tracers of star formation. We present observations using the Infrared Space Observatory of a
segment of M~31's spiral structure. Emission is compared with tracers of neutral gas (CO, HI) and stellar formation
(H\alpha, Spitzer 24 mu.) The similarity between CII maps and Ha plus 24
mu images is striking when smoothed to the same resolution, whereas the
correlation with neutral matter is much weaker. Cooling rates per H
atom increase dramatically from ~2.7e-26 ergs/s/atom in the border of surveyed regions
to ~ 1.4e-25 ergs/s/atom in zones of stellar birth. The CII/FIR(42-122)
ratio is almost constant at 2%, a factor 3 higher than typically quoted.
However, we do not believe that M~31 is unusual. Rather, whole-galaxy
fluxes used for comparisons include central areas where this ratio is known to be lower and resolved measurements neither isolate a
spiral structure nor include data as far out in disks as our measurements
presented here. A fit to published PDR models yields a plausible average
solution of G_0~100 and n~3000 for PDR radiation in zones of stellar
formation in M31's arms. These results demonstrate how localized analysis reveals properties obscured by integrated photometry and suggest that future investigations should target specific structural features rather than entire systems to properly characterize physical conditions governing atomic carbon cooling processes.
syn_max.coling::1a16d27a-89fc-4df9-8b4f-cf2532a8: We investigate a two-dimensional (2D) tight-binding framework for a topological crystalline insulator (TCI) safeguarded by rotational symmetry. The construction proceeds via stacking two Chern insulators with opposite Chern numbers which transform under conjugate representations of the rotation group, e.g. $p_\pm$ orbitals. Despite its apparent similarity to the Kane-Mele framework, it does not host stable gapless boundary modes. Nevertheless this system exhibits topological responses including the appearance of quantized fractional charge bound to rotational defects (disclinations) and the pumping of angular momentum in response to threading an elementary magnetic flux, which are described by a mutual Chern-Simons coupling between the electromagnetic gauge field and an effective gauge field corresponding to the rotational symmetry. In addition, we demonstrate that although the filled bands of this construction do not admit a symmetric Wannier representation, such obstruction is removed upon the addition of appropriate atomic orbitals, which implies 'fragile' topology. As a result, the response of the system can be derived by representing it as a superposition of atomic orbitals with positive and negative integer coefficients. Following the analysis of our construction, which serves as a prototypical example of 2D TCIs safeguarded by rotation, we demonstrate that all TCIs protected by point group symmetries which do not have protected boundary modes are either atomic insulators or fragile phases. Remarkably, this implies that gapless boundary modes exist in free electron systems if and only if there is a stable Wannier obstruction. We then use dimensional reduction to map the problem of classifying 2D TCIs safeguarded by rotation to a zero-dimensional (0D) problem which is then used to obtain the complete non-interacting classification of such TCIs as well as the reduction of this classification in the presence of interactions.
syn_max.coling::2e921a31-8ffa-4c78-8c4d-ef7e7243: We introduce a novel artificial intelligence (AI) methodology termed the 'Digital Synaptic Neural Substrate' (DSNS). This system employs selected characteristics from entities in various fields (e.g., chess puzzles, symphonic compositions, celebrated paintings) and recombines these features in such a manner as to produce fresh properties that can subsequently, in theory, be utilized to construct original items of imaginative worth to people relating to any single one of the originating disciplines. Such capability allows some burden of inventive material production to be transferred from individuals to automated systems. Our technique was evaluated in the realm of chess puzzle creation. We employed this framework to automatically devise numerous collections of chess challenges based on characteristics extracted and merged from chess conundrums and competitive matches by people, famous artworks, computer-evolved abstract imagery, snapshots of individuals, and symphonic musical recordings. The caliber of these produced chess exercises was subsequently assessed automatically using an existing and experimentally-validated computational chess aesthetics framework. They were also evaluated by skilled practitioners in the field. The findings suggest that characteristics gathered and synthesized from chess and alternative disciplines using the DSNS methodology can indeed be harnessed to automatically generate chess conundrums of reasonably elevated aesthetic merit. In particular, a low-caliber chess origin (i.e., competitive game sequences between inexperienced participants) used in conjunction with actual snapshots of humans was able to yield three-move chess exercises of comparable standard or superior to those created using a superior-caliber chess origin (i.e., published arrangements by skilled practitioners), and more efficiently as well. Why data from a foreign discipline can be integrated and operational in this fashion remains an unresolved inquiry for now. The DSNS technique is, in theory, expandable and relevant to any discipline in which entities have characteristics that can be represented using real numerical values.

The baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) feature, observed in cosmic matter
distribution at redshifts reaching approximately 3.5, reflects continued expansion of the
sonic horizon initially detected in temperature anisotropies within the cosmic
microwave background radiation. This BAO feature's location can currently be determined to better than
roughly 1% accuracy utilizing galaxies, plus 1.4-1.6% precision through Ly-alpha forests alongside
quasar clustering patterns. Combined with the Alcock-Paczyński (AP)
effect, arising from changing ratios of angular versus spatial/redshift
dimensions for presumed spherically-symmetric source distributions across distances,
such BAO determination is regarded as among the most powerful instruments available for
assessing our Universe's geometry. Within this paper, we employ five BAO feature
determinations from the final release of Sloan Digital Sky Survey IV, at
average redshifts <z>=0.38, 0.51, 0.70, 1.48 plus 2.33, to conduct a direct
head-to-head comparison between the standard cosmological model, Lambda-CDM, against one principal
competitor, known as R_h=ct cosmology. For completeness, we
complement AP diagnostic approaches with volume-averaged distance probes that assume
constant comoving scales r_d. Both diagnostic probes remain free of uncertain
parameters, such as Hubble's constant, and are therefore ideally suited for
this kind of model selection analysis. We find R_h=ct is favored by these
determinations over standard cosmology based solely on AP effects, with
likelihood approximately 75% versus roughly 25%, while Planck-Lambda-CDM is preferred over R_h=ct
relying solely on volume-averaged distance diagnostics, with likelihood near 80%
versus around 20%. A joint analysis employing both diagnostic approaches produces an inconclusive
outcome, yielding comparable likelihoods toward both cosmologies. We are consequently not
able to confirm through this work that BAO observations, on their own, support an
accelerating Universe scenario.
syn_max.coling::f4961832-eeb4-41fc-8a64-82c30107: Let me preface this by saying that I genuinely do enjoy Cowboy Bebop. The animation and designs are sublime, the soundtrack is fantastic, the action sequences are great, and when all three come together the series can occasionally become a jaw-dropping audiovisual masterpiece, particularly in the breathtaking finale. However, there exist so many problems with it that I cannot in good faith call it a "masterpiece" or proclaim it to be one of the best of the medium as anything other than a gateway program. I'll start off with the cast, which is where many of my issues lie. I'll admit, Spike and Jet are excellent protagonists, but they constitute only two-fifths of the entire Bebop Crew. Ein's introduction as a "data dog" or otherwise hyperintelligent canine goes nowhere and he spends the rest of the series just being the team's pet. Faye exhibits many of the worst characteristics that can be written about a female role; she's bossy, greedy, obsessed with her own beauty, needs to either be rescued or is a hindrance to the group more often than an asset, she frequently wears revealing clothing for the sole purpose of fanservice. Ed is hit or miss, and walks the line between endearing and annoying, but hardly receives much development beyond her introductory episode. The main villain Vicious is especially bad. He has very little personality and motivation aside from a desire for more power, and even though the narrative goes a bit into his backstory it never establishes what drives him. At the end of the program, Vicious remains little more than an evil guy in a black coat with enough fighting skill that it makes Spike struggle to land a bullet in him, aside from the obvious fact that Vicious becomes a representation of the syndicate our protagonist ran away from. As a result the five episodes that involve him (Sympathy for the Devil, Jupiter Jazz parts one and two, and Real Folk Blues parts one and two) don't leave me feeling as if they are as spectacular as the creators want me to feel like they deliver. Aside from that, the quality of individual installments varies dramatically. For an episodic program that only has about five chapters that build an overall story, that's saying a lot. Sure, there are fantastic entries such as Waltz for Venus and Ganymede Elegy, but there are also fairly ho-hum offerings such as Bohemian Rhapsody, Speak Like a Child, and Boogie Woogie Feng Shui. syn_max.coling::6ea6d618-d59e-455d-a265-490e1418: Multiple factors can cause software to fail unexpectedly. Here are several frequent culprits: Division by zero: You may recall from elementary school mathematics that dividing numbers by zero is impossible. The outcome remains undefined. Well, if software instructs the machine to perform this invalid operation, the system will notify the application that it is attempting something incorrect. If the application cannot manage that circumstance, it may terminate abruptly. Access violation: Software is only permitted to utilize certain memory regions. Other areas are forbidden. If an application attempts to utilize forbidden memory regions, the system will notify the application that it is attempting something incorrect. If the application cannot manage that circumstance, it may terminate abruptly. Deadlock: Let's say you and your pal Tommy are playing with toys. You possess the crimson block, and Tommy possesses the azure block. You desire to exchange blocks, so you inform Tommy that you will relinquish the crimson block after he relinquishes the azure block. Tommy informs you that he will relinquish the azure block after you relinquish the crimson block. Both of you will remain there indefinitely awaiting the other person to surrender their possession, and you will never accomplish anything. That is a deadlock circumstance, and when it occurs inside software, the application becomes unresponsive and there is nothing you can do except terminate it and restart it. Unhandled exception: Sometimes software will incorporate a special kind of error verification mechanism. When an error is detected, one component of the software raises an exception, and another component of the software is expected to intercept the exception and address it. If an exception gets raised and is not intercepted by any component of the software, then usually a dialog will appear informing you that a difficulty was not addressed properly, and the software will shut down. All of these circumstances are caused by "bugs" in the software. "Bugs" are simply components of the software that are not written correctly, or don't account for every possible thing that can occur. Some software has more "bugs" than other software. Why? Maybe because the developers who wrote the software were in more of a hurry or didn't test it as thoroughly as they should have, or because the software is so intricate that it is challenging to address every possible circumstance that might occur.','Think of software as "a method to accomplish tasks" - a typical example given is how to make a peanut butter and jelly sandwich. Your initial routine might read: obtain bread obtain peanut butter obtain jelly obtain knife spread peanut butter on one slice spread jelly on other slice combine bread together SERVE If you exhaust peanut butter supplies, you're stuck midway through the directions without anywhere remaining to proceed - that's a failure. A more intricate routine would describe how a pizza restaurant operates - there's more ingredients, more methods to mix them, you have a lot of different employees arriving and departing at the same moment a bunch more situations that can fail. There's situations that can fail you can resolve situations that cannot be resolved - situations that cannot be resolved (or developers are too indolent to resolve) are failures.

syn_max.coling::a9b058a8-5ce8-448f-820a-6ffba640: Because of the camera's field of view (FOV). If you're a big first person shooter game player (or you know about cameras) you're probably familiar with FOV. If we consider what we can perceive as a cone starting at our eye and expanding outward like [this] (URL0) then FOV is the angle between the two boundary lines. In shooter games FOV is often expanded by pros to gain an advantage, since it lets you observe more of your surroundings. [Here] (URL1) is a quick example of increasing a game's FOV I googled up. The picture on the left has the FOV expanded to 65 degrees compared to the default of 45 degrees on the right. With the larger FOV you can witness more on the left and right sides. But you'll also notice that the 2 trailer things look like they're farther away even though the player is standing in the same place - that's because as you increase the FOV you also change how the light from distant objects is going to converge on your 2D surface. Essentially a larger FOV means that objects seem to decrease in dimensions faster as they get farther away. The opposite is also true, if you reduce the FOV then it increases the apparent magnitude of far away objects since they now converge on a larger portion of the viewing area. The camera on DSCOVR used to capture these pictures has a FOV of just 0.61deg. It makes it very effective at collecting illumination from remote objects because it is focused on a very small cone. It also means that the distance between Earth and Moon doesn't have the same effect on relative proportions as it does when photographed with a regular lens or human vision.," "Hold your hand in front of your face. It's probably about as big as your monitor. Keep your palm in the identical spot and move your head backwards. Your appendage now appears smaller than the screen. There's a certain distance where your mitt and the display get tinier together, at the matching rate. This occurs because the distance between you and those two things becomes a lot greater than the separation between those two items. Angular diameter depends on distance, and ratio of distances. Basically, the first photograph is very close to the moon and far from the earth, so the satellite seems enormous. The second snapshot is very remote from both the planet and the lunar body, so they appear like their actual relative sizes. So yes, the globe DOES appear diminished in the second depiction, but the celestial companion got smaller a lot faster just like your extremity.," "DSCOVR basically had its camera zoomed in more. The EPIC instrument on the spacecraft that captured the photograph is specifically designed to observe our world from a distance, whereas the cameras on the Apollo missions were more general purpose. To be more precise, in a photographic device the focal length of the optics determines the physical dimensions of the representation formed on the sensor. Then the physical extent of the detector determines the field of coverage, and the pixel resolution of the recording surface determines the magnitude of each individual pixel in the resulting picture. With analogue film there are no pixels but the emulsion still has a resolution limit because of its chemistry and there's also a clarity threshold imposed by the glass elements. Finally a large photograph can simply be cropped, although the DSCOVR rendering is in fact pretty much its full dimensions.
syn_max.coling::3dd39352-d471-4ab9-bd50-b7345fc1: You can call what you're requesting information about a 'prosperity levy', or 'asset taxation'. These are impositions not based on earnings you generated in a given year, but some measure of how much you possess. Some nations (Italy I believe is a prime example) impose levies on ownership of foreign land. Some countries assess amounts possessed by corporations [Canada did this until approximately five to ten years ago depending on province]. Some jurisdictions strictly charge your net worth above a certain threshold (Switzerland, as has been mentioned, does this). One form of what you are referring to that does exist in the US is the 'Estate Duty'. This is an imposition on the amount of prosperity that a person possesses, at the moment they perish. The floor for when this charge applies has been very volatile over the last two decades, but it is generally in the multi-millions, and I believe sits somewhere around five million dollars. If these impositions start to crop up more and more (and I believe they will), don't be shocked at the initial 'sticker price'. Theoretically a prosperity levy could replace some of the current earnings assessment regime in many nations without creating a strict increased burden on their populace. For instance: if you owe ten thousand dollars in salary-based charges this year, but a two-thousand-dollar asset levy is instituted next year, then you are still in the same position as long as your wage-based obligation is reduced to eight thousand. Whether these levies are effective or preferable is really a question of economics, not personal finance, so I will not belabour that point. Note: if the money you have saved generates returns (interest, or dividends, or maybe rent from a condominium you possess), then those returns are typically assessed alongside your employment compensation. Any 'prosperity or asset imposition' as I've described it above would be in addition to charges on investment returns.
syn_max.coling::8eb96c1a-6193-4f0f-843b-4b91efbe: You could have both positions exercised (and assigned to you) on the same trading session, but I don't think you could lose funds on both during that identical period. The reason is that while exercises are immediate, assignments are processed after markets close at the end of each session. See http://www.888options.com/help/faq/assignment.jsp for details. So you would get both assignments simultaneously, that evening. The net effect should be that you don't own any shares (someone would put you the equity, then it'd be called away) and you don't have the contracts anymore. You should have incoming funds of $1500 selling the shares to the call exerciser and outgoing cash of $1300 buying from the put exerciser, right? So you would have no more contracts but $200 additional cash in your account in the morning. You bought at 13 and sold at 15. This position is an agreement to purchase at 13 and sell at 15 at someone else's choice. The way you lose capital is if one of the contracts isn't exercised while the other is, i.e. if the equity is below 13 so nobody is going to opt to purchase from you at 15, but they'll sell to you at 13; or above 15 so nobody is going to opt to sell to you at 13, but they'll buy from you at 15. You make profit if neither is exercised (you keep the premium you sold for) or both are exercised (you keep the gap between the two, plus the premium). Having both exercised is surely rare, since early exercise is uncommon to begin with, and tends to happen when derivatives are deep in the money; so you'd expect both to be acted upon if both are deep in the money at some moment. Having both be acted upon on the same trading day... can't be common, but it's maybe most likely just before expiration with minimal time value remaining, if the underlying moves around quickly so both derivatives are in the money at some point during that session.
syn_max.coling::59aec439-babf-4d21-b03b-4f331a96: The initial step you must take involves examining your agreement and stipulations of your plastic money, or inquiring with your financial institution, regarding how they handle incoming remittances. As Dilip notes in his response, in America, they will likely direct the minimum remittance toward the lower interest obligation, and then must channel the remainder above the minimum toward the higher interest obligation. In other nations, this will vary by statute and practice. Do not assume it will retire the higher obligation, or proportionally, without inquiring. Let's consider the following illustration. You are indebted $6000. $5000 is at 13.5% (normal purchase interest) and $1000 is at 22% (cash withdrawal interest). If your financial institution directs remittances to both obligations proportionally, then a remittance of $600 will reduce your purchase obligation by $500 and your cash withdrawal obligation by $100. The mean APR, then, is simply sum of the product of the APR times obligation. So here, (.135*5000 + .225*1000)/6000 = 15%. This is called a weighted mean. If the institution directs the remittance differently - such as toward the lower interest first, or some specified part toward the lower interest and the remainder toward the higher interest - then this will be misleading if you enter it into a computation tool, because your mean APR will climb over duration as you retire the purchase obligation but don't retire the cash withdrawal obligation, or may decline if the opposite occurs. The weighted mean is probably reasonably accurate in the circumstance that you describe, even if you have rules directing the obligation differently, so long as they don't 100% retire the lower interest - so it may be the simplest option for you in terms of rough computations (where it's not critical to be precise, just approximate). One method using the online computation tools that might be superior, is to treat these like two separate debts/plastic money accounts. Many computation tools exist for multiple obligations. Then you can allocate funds differently to the two 'plastic money accounts'. This would permit you to see how long you will need until you've retired the higher obligation, for illustration, although it probably won't perfectly match things - unless you locate a website that has this specific feature available you probably will have to either live with a small discrepancy in your computations or perform the arithmetic by hand.

This manuscript extends Lenc&Vedaldi15's study, demonstrating that CNN feature encodings at the FC7 stage exhibit partial equivariance toward various categories of geometric manipulations, and that training with particular transformation groups enhances representational equivalence.

The authors conducted an impressive quantity of experiments, building over thirty networks employing different augmentation strategies. Nevertheless, identifying the central contribution proves challenging. While the researchers examined properties at an alternative stage compared to Lenc&Vedaldi15's investigation, discovering novel insights beyond the established understanding that augmentation promotes invariance remains difficult. Although the evaluation appears mostly sound, the manuscript doesn't adequately address the challenge advertised in its heading.

Primary concerns emerge in the experiments examining representational distances:
* Selecting exclusively FC7 seems controversial—it precedes only one classification stage (FC8) before reaching the final output—class probabilities. Since FC8 constitutes merely linear projection, the equivalence mapping essentially re-projects the FC8 parameters of the attached model onto the original model's parameters. Conducting comparable experiments across multiple stages might prove more valuable (given that models are already trained).
* The experiment measuring representational distance omits classification accuracy on the testing dataset. Such information would clarify whether the feature encodings are genuinely compatible under linear transformations...
* For the K-NN experiment, whether measurements occur per individual test example remains unclear. After learning the equivalence mapping? More illuminating would be demonstrating that models trained on comparable augmentation transformation groups achieve greater compatibility on the target challenge.
* The suggested approach fails to enhance equivariance reliably across all challenges. Particularly with \lambda_1 and \lambda_2 having such minimal magnitudes, the objective function essentially equals simple augmentation since it merely accumulates the objective from the unmodified and manipulated input. Perhaps the problem lies in choosing the FC7 stage?

Overall, this manuscript presents some intriguing findings regarding FC7 equivariance, yet fails to extract many compelling fresh observations from these experiments. Given certain problems with the equivalence investigations and the fine-tuning of equivariance, I cannot recommend accepting this submission. However, refining the investigations on previously trained models and restructuring this document into more exploratory research might yield valuable contributions to the discipline.

Several minor problems also exist:
* Experimental verification that the novel criterion for equivariance mapping produces superior outcomes is absent.
* The angular measurements on pages one and five lack units (degrees?).
* On page three, "In practice, it is difficult...", what gets maximised/minimised isn't M_g itself, but rather the objective function over M_g
* Page four, footnote two—if you're simply halving the activations, calling it dropout seems questionable since this constant multiplier can be absorbed into the subsequent/previous parameters
* Does the architecture for RVL-CDIP match Alexnet's structure?
* On page seven, Figure 3a+3b—in my view, rendering the diagonal entries white proves highly misleading, and possibly even erroneous, since the distance separating identical feature encodings should equal zero (which also provides verification that experiments are executed correctly).

Appreciation for an intriguing contribution. I personally favor the information bottleneck framework and am delighted to witness its utilization within deep neural architectures. To my understanding, this represents the initial manuscript applying IB for training multilayer systems (the foundational publications merely introduced the concept), though see below regarding the notation about concurrent research.

The derivation establishing the variational lowerbound appears exceptionally lucid, even for readers unfamiliar with variational techniques. Additionally, the explanation concerning the IB framework remains transparent. Experimental outcomes appear quite promising.

I discovered the exposition regarding the architecture somewhat perplexing. Within variational techniques/information maximisation, p typically designates the generative system while q signifies the "recognition engine". This implies the selection of recognition methodology remains separate from the modeling approach. Nevertheless, the introduced VIB assumed p(x, y) as the **underlying empirical distribution** (and estimated via the sample distribution), thus here the architecture actually becomes q(y|z)p(z|x). Subsequently, the contributors introduced p(y|x) as the **forecasting distribution** on page 8, paragraph 2 within section 4.2.3. Forecasting in what manner? I suspect you intended p(y|x) = \int q(y|z) p(z|x) dz under these circumstances, yet this renders the two characterizations contradictory to one another!

The contributors have established an intriguing relationship to variational auto-encoders and the warm-up procedure (via tuning beta). Nevertheless, even when the objective formula matches the variational lowerbound employed in VAE (under these conditions beta = 1), the underlying architecture differs! For instance, r(z) within VIB constitutes the variational estimate to p(z) (which indicates r(z) isn't a constituent within the architecture), whereas in VAE it constitutes the prior probability which is genuinely specified during the modeling stage. Similarly, p(z|x) within VIB is incorporated into the architecture, whereas in VAE that constitutes the approximate posterior and can be independently selected (e.g., you might employ p(x|z) as a multilayer NN but p(z|x) as a multilayer NN or a Gaussian process).

In conclusion, I believe the exposition concerning the modeling approach lacks clarity. I hope these points would be rendered more transparent in revision since the current exposition makes me uneasy as a Bayesian practitioner. Within the VAE section, it's preferable to explicitly mention the distinction between VIB and VAE, and supply some intuitions if the VIB interpretation is favored.

Errors:
Eq. 9-11: did you intend q(y|z) rather than q(z|y)?
Fig 2 "as beta becomes smaller": did you intend "larger"?

**notation for concurrent research**
The contributors claimed that the submission represented an independent effort to Chalk et al. 2016 which is online since May 2016. It appears to me that contemporary deep learning scholarship is extremely competitive that numerous researchers publish identical ideas simultaneously. So I would accept this assertion and commend the contributors' integrity, but should this not be accurate, I would not endorse the submission for publication.

This manuscript presents an MT training corpus selection method scoring and
ranking general-domain phrases via CNN classification. Comparison against previous work

remains uncertain whether the authors also evaluated against bilingual dataset selection (e.g.
summed differences of cross-entropy measures).
The rationale for employing a CNN rather than an RNN/LSTM was initially unclear to me, but
it constitutes a merit of this study to argue that certain portions of a text/sentence
carry greater importance than others and this is accomplished through CNNs. Nevertheless, the
manuscript does not experimentally demonstrate whether a BOW or SEQ (or their combination)
representation is more critical and for what reasons.
The textual explanation of the CNN architecture (one-hot or semi-supervised utilizing
pre-trained embeddings) 
is lucid, thorough, and highlights the crucial aspects. Nevertheless, a diagram of
the layers illustrating how inputs are merged would be worth a thousand statements.
The manuscript is generally well composed, but some parentheses for citations are not
required (\citet vs. \citep) (e.g line 385).
Experiments and evaluation substantiate the assertions of the study, but I am somewhat
concerned regarding the procedure for determining the quantity of selected in-domain
phrases (line 443) based on a separate validation corpus:
- What validation material is employed here? It is also unclear on what dataset
hyperparameters of the CNN architectures are chosen. How sensitive are the architectures to
this?
- Table 2 should really contrast performance of different techniques with the identical
quantity of phrases selected. As Figure 1 demonstrates, the technique of the manuscript
still appears to outperform the baselines in this scenario.

- I would be interested in an experiment that contrasts the methodology of the
manuscript against baselines when more in-domain material is available, not just the
development corpus.
- The findings or discussion portion could feature some example phrases
selected by the various techniques to substantiate the assertions made in section 5.4.
- Regarding the argument of abstracting away from surface forms in 5.4:
Another baseline to contrast against could have been the research of Axelrod, 2015,
who replaces some terms with POS tags to reduce LM dataset sparsity to see whether
the word2vec embeddings provide an additional advantage over this approach.
- Employing the summation of source and target classification performance is very similar to
source & target Lewis-Moore LM dataset selection: summation of differences of
cross-entropy measures. A citation to this research around line 435 would be reasonable.
Finally, I wonder if you could learn weights for the summation of both source &
target classification performance by extending the CNN architecture to the
bilingual/parallel setting, enabling joint optimization across language pairs for improved filtering outcomes.

Photovoltaic energy represents a marvel of contemporary engineering. There exists one minuscule difficulty, nevertheless. It remains costlier than utilizing alternative methods of generating electricity. If expense wasn't an issue, this technology would constitute a superior choice, but that applies to every form of sustainable energy source.

Numerous individuals will note that establishing photovoltaic systems is comparable with or even less expensive than constructing fresh generating facilities, such as atomic or fossil-fuel stations. While accurate on very large scales, you're probably not going to erect your personal electricity plant, and therefore lack that expenditure to grapple with.

Examine the price of a photovoltaic array versus how much electricity *on average* it can generate. Calculate the numbers.

> I believe if the government invested some money they could easily shut down one or two nuclear power plants

You seem to be laboring under some false assumptions. Firstly, the administration is subsidizing photovoltaic purchases in California in a huge way - so they *are* investing some funds. Secondly, the authorities do not operate the Atomic Generating Stations - those are run by private corporations. They are *regulated* by federal agencies. Also, the primary expense of an atomic facility is the construction of the installation and the disposal of the radioactive material - not the operation of the station itself. Closing a functioning installation would waste funds, not save resources.

Like I said, I love photovoltaic technology, for all kinds of reasons. It's "point of use" which means there is very little loss due to long distance transmission. It's practically zero emissions. It's silent (that's a big thing for me). It provides the greatest benefit when the need is highest, in summer, in daytime.

Possibly the best application of photovoltaics might be to operate air conditioning. During summer when the sun is strong, the demand for cooling is intense. Utilize the illumination provided by photovoltaic arrays to help chill the structure. Additionally, if the arrays are on the rooftop, they provide shade for the structure. Win/win.

Still, on a pure expense/benefit analysis, nevertheless, it remains less costly to utilize fossil fuels or methane to supply electricity.

Say you're a merchant living in 17th century Amsterdam, and there's a bunch of super-rich ladies who really, really love cumin (as in, the spice). Unfortunately, this aromatic seed doesn't grow anywhere near your Dutch city; you have to go to the middle east or India to obtain some of that fine stuff so it's *super-expensive*. Over there, however, it flourishes like a weed and costs very little money. If only you could get some of that cheap seasoning over to your home port, you could make a lot of cash!

Unfortunately, the only way to accomplish that is to send out a big-ass vessel for like nine months. Not only is that HUGELY expensive (you have to acquire a sailing craft, and a captain plus crew who all want nine months worth of pay), but it is also really risky. The boat could sink, after all, or all the fragrant seeds could spoil.

So how do you achieve this goal? Assuming you're not stupendously wealthy yourself (and very few people or groups, aside from maybe whole nations, possess that kind of fortune), how do you finance this voyage? You could go to a bank or money-lender and take out a loan, which would have a very steep interest rate that could almost eat up all of your profits. And what if the ship sank? You'd be completely bankrupt, and be thrown into prison, if the creditor doesn't waste your broke ass first.

So, you come up with an idea. You can't finance this journey alone. But you could rather easily cover, say, one tenth of the expense of the expedition. And look at that, you have nine friends, all of whom could also afford one tenth of the necessary funds. So you all come to an agreement: you decide to each contribute part of the required sum for the trip (i.e. you "buy stock" in the enterprise), each getting shares worth one tenth of the total venture. With this pooled capital, you pay for the vessel and sailors, send them off, and then nine months later, it returns with a cargo-hold full of delicious, super-expensive aromatic seeds. The profits far and away compensate for the initial outlay, and each of you and your companions gets one tenth of the enormous returns.

But what happens if your ship sinks? Well, it's a real bummer obviously (especially for the crew!), but you only paid for one tenth of the expense, and this was an amount you could afford to eat; you're not gonna get killed over it. Since the danger was spread around to ten people, no one landed in debtors prison. Everyone took a small hit, instead of one person taking an enormous blow.

Think about this example, and all the individuals involved in it. The fancy ladies got their desired spice (and for cheaper than they would have otherwise). The shipwrights got work building a new vessel. The captain and sailors all received employment and a salary. The trader in India gained a new customer for his fragrant commodity. And obviously, you and your companions got really wealthy in the process. In short, *every single person is better off*, and it wouldn't have happened if this notion of "buying and selling shares" didn't exist.

This is the advantage of equity markets. They move capital around from where it just lies around doing absolutely nothing to where it can be put to productive use, and in the meantime, everybody gets richer. Such systems also distribute danger between lots of individuals, so you don't have to be afraid of going broke all the time.

Now, obviously, there are problems with how the modern day American version of equity trading functions. But the critique is that it stopped doing what it is supposed to be doing (i.e. allocating resources so that they can be put into productive employment) and stopped being a means to an end, instead becoming an end unto itself. The basic concept of organized share exchanges is a fantastic idea, and you'd have to be a real hard-core communist to oppose such arrangements. These mechanisms are why we have railroads, cars, computers, telephones, cheap and plentiful food, medicine, and all the other contemporary things we value so highly today.

Depends on whether your enterprise operates as a sole proprietorship, single-owner limited liability company, multiple-owner limited liability corporation, an entity with the "S" taxation election, an Subchapter-S organization, or a Subchapter-C establishment.

Sole Proprietorship: All earnings and deficits pass to you individually. You're also personally liable for anything that goes wrong. Pro Tip: establish an LLC or go get a free consultation with a commercial attorney.

Single-Owner Limited Liability Company: Earnings and deficits flow through to you personally, but your liability remains limited to the firm's assets. You also must pay self-employment taxation.

Multiple-Owner Limited Liability Corporation: Earnings and deficits are split in proportion to each member's ownership stake in the venture. You also remit self-employment levies.

Entity with "S" Election: You compensate yourself a reasonable wage, and that wage isn't subject to the self-employment levy. Remaining earnings and deficits are passed through to you and any other investors in proportion to each investor's percentage stake in the organization. Whether or not you get taxed on any distributions depends on your basis, but this is where things become complicated and I can't ELI5 (just let the accountant worry about this)

Subchapter-S Organization: see above

Subchapter-C Establishment: The firm's earnings are taxed at the organizational taxation level and then any dividends made to investors are taxed as well. This is called double taxation and it's why these establishments are not ideal for small enterprise owners.

syn_max.coling::817b2dbf-699e-4bec-825a-2bbdf598: An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) represents a crucial cybersecurity instrument for network administrators as it identifies malicious traffic and cyberattacks. With recent successes of artificial intelligence techniques such as deep neural networks, increasingly more IDS now employ computational intelligence algorithms to detect intrusions faster. However, these mechanisms lack robustness when facing previously unseen types of threats. With growing numbers of novel intrusions, especially against Internet of Things equipment, having a resilient IDS able to spot unusual and fresh threats becomes necessary. This work explores possibilities of leveraging generative adversarial models to enhance the resilience of computational intelligence based IDS. More specifically, we propose a novel method named SIGMA, that harnesses adversarial examples to strengthen IDS against emerging categories of intrusions. Using Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) and metaheuristics, SIGMA produces adversarial instances, iteratively, and utilizes them to retrain a computational intelligence-based IDS, until convergence of detection rate occurs (i.e. until the identification mechanism stops improving anymore). A round of enhancement consists of a generative phase, in which we employ GANs and metaheuristics to produce samples; an evaluation stage in which we calculate the identification rate of those newly produced intrusions; and a training phase, in which we instruct the IDS with those threats. We have evaluated the SIGMA approach for four standard computational intelligence classification procedures acting as IDS, with a combination of GAN and a hybrid local-search plus genetic procedure, to create fresh datasets of intrusions. Our results show that SIGMA can successfully produce adversarial threats against different computational intelligence based IDS. Also, utilizing SIGMA, we can boost the performance of an IDS up to one hundred percent after as little as two rounds of enhancement, demonstrating significant practical value for security professionals.
syn_max.coling::0a6f4d1d-1792-4bfc-a4cf-9fcf0636: Phylogenetic networks are leaf-labelled directed acyclic graphs employed to describe non-treelike evolutionary histories and thus represent a generalization of phylogenetic hierarchies. The hybridization value of such a structure equals the sum of all indegrees minus the quantity of vertices plus one. The Hybridization Value challenge takes as input a collection of phylogenetic hierarchies and asks to construct a structure that contains an embedding of each supplied hierarchy and has a smallest possible reticulation count. We present an algorithm for the Reticulation Count challenge on three binary phylogenetic hierarchies with n leaves, which runs in time O ( c^k poly (n, where k denotes the reticulation value of an optimal structure and c some positive constant. For the case of two hierarchies, an approach with running duration O ( 3.18^k n) was proposed before whereas an approach with running duration O ( c^k poly (n for more than two hierarchies had prior to this article remained elusive. The method for two hierarchies uses the close connection to acyclic agreement forests to achieve a linear exponent in the running duration, while previous methods for more than two hierarchies (explicitly or implicitly) relied on a brute force search through all possible underlying topologies, leading to running durations that are not O ( c^k poly (n, for any constant. The connection to acyclic agreement forests is much weaker for more than two hierarchies, so even given the right agreement forest, the reconstruction of the structure poses major challenges. We prove novel structural insights that allow us to reconstruct a structure without having to guess the underlying topology. Our techniques generalize to more than three supplied hierarchies with the exception of one key lemma that maps vertices in the structure to hierarchy vertices and, thus, minimizes the amount of guessing involved in constructing the structure. The main open challenge therefore is to prove insights that establish such a mapping for more than three supplied hierarchies.

syn_max.coling::a098aa01-9d81-40a6-8321-ca3d4a88: Graph-Laplacians along with their spectral embeddings occupy a crucial position across numerous domains within machine learning. This paper concentrates on graph-Laplacian dimension reduction for spectral partitioning of datasets as a principal application; however, these techniques can additionally be utilized in information mining, manifold discovery, etc. Spectral embedding furnishes a low-dimensional parametrization of dataset geometry which renders the subsequent operation (e.g., partitioning via k-means or any variant thereof) considerably simpler. Nevertheless, despite reducing dimensionality, the overall computational expense may remain prohibitively high for massive collections owing to two factors. First, computing partial eigendecomposition of the graph-Laplacian typically necessitates a large Krylov subspace. Second, after spectral embedding concludes, one must still handle the same quantity of points, which may undermine the efficiency of this approach. For instance, partitioning embedded information is usually performed with various relaxations of k-means whose computational burden scales poorly relative to collection size. Also, these methods become prone to getting stuck in local minima, so their robustness depends on initial guess selection. In this work, we shift attention from the entire collection to a subset of vertices (target subset). We develop two novel procedures for such low-dimensional representation of the original network that preserves important global distances between nodes within the target subset. In particular, this allows ensuring that target subset partitioning is consistent with spectral partitioning of the complete collection if one would perform such. That is achieved by a properly parametrized reduced-order model (ROM) of the graph-Laplacian that approximates accurately diffusion transfer function of the original network for inputs and outputs restricted to the target subset. Operating with a small target subset reduces greatly the required dimension of Krylov subspace and permits exploitation of conventional procedures (like variants of k-means) in regimes when they are most robust and efficient. This was verified in numerical partitioning experiments with both synthetic and real information. We also note that our ROM technique can be utilized in a purely transfer-function-data-driven manner, so it becomes the only feasible option for extremely large networks that are not directly accessible. There are several uses for our procedures. First, they can be employed independently for representative subset partitioning in cases when handling the complete network is either infeasible or simply not required. Second, they may be utilized for quality control. Third, as they drastically reduce problem size, they enable application of more sophisticated procedures for the operation under consideration (like more powerful variants of k-means based on semi-definite programming (SDP) instead of conventional Lloyd's procedure). Finally, they can serve as building blocks of a multi-level divide-and-conquer type procedure to handle the complete network. The latter will be reported in a separate article.

The parameters n , k , r , t are positive integers such that r k n and t - n k . We examine the functional restoration model and the sequential strategy for restoring multiple failing nodes. By functional restoration, we mean that the packet stored in each newcomer is not necessarily an exact duplicate of the vanished data but a symbol that preserves the (r , t) -local restoration property. By the sequential strategy, we mean that the t newcomers are ordered in a proper sequence such that each newcomer can be restored from the live nodes and the newcomers that are ordered before it. We also give some constructions of exact LRCs for t {2 , 3 } whose length n achieves the boundary of (n , k , r , t) -FLRC, which proves the tightness of our boundaries and also implies that there is no gap between the optimal code length of functional LRCs and exact LRCs for certain sets of parameters. Moreover, our constructions are over the binary field, hence are of interest in practice. This demonstrates that achieving optimal performance does not require sacrificing exactness properties under specific parameter configurations, making these approaches particularly valuable for real-world implementations.

In practice, parity and democratic governance are deficient because elected representatives in the Parliament cannot initiate laws against the Commission's wishes, inhabitants of smallest countries possess ten times the voting weight in Parliament compared to residents of largest nations, and "qualified majorities" or consensus within the Council are required for lawmaking. Justification for this "democratic deficit" under Treaties is usually thought being that completion integration of continental economy plus political institutions required technical coordination by experts, while popular understanding of the EU developed and nationalist sentiments declined post-war. Over time, this has meant the Parliament gradually assumed more voice: from being an unelected assembly, to its first direct elections in 1979, to possessing increasingly greater rights in lawmaking procedures. Citizens' entitlements are therefore limited compared to democratic polities within all member states: under TEU article 11 inhabitants and associations possess entitlements such as publicising their views plus submit initiatives that must be considered by the Commission with one million signatures. TFEU article 227 contains a further entitlement for residents to petition the Parliament on issues affecting them. Parliamentary elections take place every five years, and votes for Members of the European Parliament in member states must be organised by proportional representation or a single transferable ballot. There are 750 MEPs and their numbers are "degressively proportional" according to member state size. This means - although the Council is meant being the body representing member states - in the Parliament inhabitants of smaller nations possess more voice than residents in larger countries. MEPs divide, as they do in national Parliaments, along political party lines: the conservative European People's Party currently is largest, while the Party of European Socialists leads opposition. Parties do not receive public funds from the EU, as the Court of Justice held in Parti ecologiste "Les Verts" v Parliament that this was entirely an issue to be regulated by member states. The Parliament's powers include calling inquiries into maladministration or appointing an Ombudsman pending any court proceedings. It can require the Commission respond to questions and by a two-thirds majority can censure the whole Commission (as happened to the Santer Commission in 1999). In some cases, the Parliament has explicit consultation entitlements, which the Commission must genuinely follow. However its role participation in lawmaking procedures still remains limited because no representative can actually propose or pass laws without the Commission plus Council, meaning power kratia is not in hands of directly elected representatives of the people demos: in the EU it is not yet true that "administration is in hands of many and not of few."
syn_max.coling::049da962-b4ab-4271-80d7-6c08dd71: Despite Martin Luther's harsh polemics against his Roman Catholic opponents over issues concerning Mary and the saints, theologians appear to agree that Luther adhered to the Marian decrees of the ecumenical councils and dogmas of the church. A cryptographic signature constitutes a mathematical scheme for verifying authenticity of electronic messages or documents. A valid cryptographic signature, where prerequisites are satisfied, gives a recipient very high confidence that the communication was created by a known sender (authenticity), and that the transmission was not altered in transit (integrity).

Cryptographic signatures are a standard element of most protocol suites, and are commonly employed for software distribution, financial transactions, contract management applications, and in other cases where it is important to detect forgery or tampering.

Such signatures are often utilized to implement electronic signatures, which includes any electronic data that carries the intent of a signature, but not all electronic signatures use cryptographic signatures. Electronic signatures have legal significance in some countries, including Canada, South Africa, the United States, Algeria, Turkey, India, Brazil, Indonesia, Mexico, Saudi Arabia,[10] Uruguay,[11] Switzerland, Chile[12] and the nations of the European Union.[13][14]

These mechanisms employ asymmetric cryptography. In many instances, they provide a layer of validation and security to communications sent through a non-secure channel: Properly implemented, such a mechanism gives the receiver reason to believe the transmission was dispatched by the claimed sender. Such mechanisms are equivalent to traditional handwritten signatures in many respects, but properly executed versions are more difficult to forge than the handwritten type. These schemes, in the sense utilized here, are cryptographically based, and must be executed properly to be effective. They can also provide non-repudiation, meaning that the signer cannot successfully claim they did not authorize a communication, while also claiming their private key remains secret.[15] Further, some non-repudiation approaches offer a timestamp for the signature, so that even if the private key is exposed, the authorization is valid.[16][17] Signed communications may be anything representable as a bitstring: examples include electronic mail, contracts, or a transmission dispatched via some other protocol.

Vocal pattern identification constitutes an interdisciplinary subfield within information technology and computational linguistics, developing methodologies plus technologies enabling recognition alongside translation for uttered language toward written form via machines, with primary advantages being searchability. Alternative names include automatic vocal pattern identification (ASR), machine utterance interpretation, or talk-to-writing (STT). This domain incorporates knowledge plus research from information processing, linguistic studies, and digital engineering disciplines. The inverse procedure involves vocal synthesis.

Certain vocal pattern identification arrangements require "training" (alternatively termed "enrollment") whereby individual speakers read passages or isolated vocabulary toward the arrangement. The arrangement analyzes each person's specific vocalization, using this data for fine-tuning interpretation regarding that individual's utterances, yielding increased accuracy. Arrangements lacking such training bear the label "speaker-independent" configurations. Arrangements employing such preparation receive designation as "speaker dependent."

Vocal pattern identification applications encompass auditory user interfaces like number dialing (e.g., "telephone residence"), routing incoming communications (e.g., "I desire making a reverse-charge telephone communication"), domotic appliance management, keyword searches (e.g., locating a podcast containing particular phrases), simple information entry (e.g., inputting a payment card number), preparation for structured documentation (e.g., a radiology summary), determining orator characteristics, talk-toward-writing processing (e.g., word processors or electronic mail), plus aircraft operations (usually designated direct auditory input).

The phrase "vocal recognition" or orator identification denotes identifying who is speaking, rather than their message content. Identifying the orator can simplify translating utterances within arrangements that received training on a particular individual's vocalization, or this capability can authenticate or verify an orator's identity as part of a security procedure.

From the technological perspective, vocal pattern identification possesses a lengthy history containing several waves of major innovations. Most recently, the discipline has benefited from progress in neural network learning and massive dataset analysis. These advances are evidenced not solely by the surge of scholarly publications issued within the discipline, but more significantly by worldwide commercial adoption of varied neural network learning approaches in designing and deploying vocal pattern identification arrangements across industries globally.

Regulation science represents a mathematical discipline addressing the governance of dynamic mechanisms within engineered procedures and apparatus. Its purpose involves developing a framework or algorithm governing how mechanism inputs get applied for driving the mechanism toward a preferred condition, while minimizing any lag, excess response, or persistent deviation and guaranteeing a degree of governance stability; frequently aiming to accomplish a measure of optimal performance.

Achieving this requires a regulator possessing the necessary corrective characteristics. Such a regulator monitors the governed procedure variable (PV), comparing it against the reference or target point (SP). The discrepancy between actual and intended magnitude of the procedure variable, termed the deviation signal, or SP-PV discrepancy, gets utilized as feedback for generating a regulatory action bringing the governed procedure variable to identical magnitude as the target point. Additional aspects receiving study include controllability and observability. Regulation science finds application in governance mechanism engineering for designing automation that has revolutionized manufacturing, aviation, telecommunications and additional industries, while creating novel disciplines like robotics.

Extensive utilization typically occurs of a diagrammatic approach called the block representation. Within it, the transfer relationship, alternatively designated the mechanism relationship or network relationship, constitutes a mathematical framework of the connection linking the input and output founded on the differential equations characterizing the mechanism.

Regulation science originates from the nineteenth century, when the theoretical foundation for the functioning of speed controllers was initially characterized by James Clerk Maxwell. Regulation science received further advancement by Edward Routh in 1874, Charles Sturm and in 1895, Adolf Hurwitz, who all contributed toward establishing governance stability criteria; and from 1922 onward, the emergence of PID regulation science by Nicolas Minorsky.

Although a primary utilization of mathematical regulation science lies in governance mechanisms engineering, addressing the creation of procedure regulation mechanisms for industry, additional utilizations extend far beyond this. As the broad science of feedback mechanisms, regulation science proves valuable wherever feedback manifests—thus regulation science also possesses utilizations in biological sciences, computing engineering, sociology and operational research.

Pharmaceutical design, frequently termed rational medication development or simply logical creation, is the inventive procedure of discovering novel therapeutics based on understanding a biological target. The medication is most commonly an organic small molecule that activates or inhibits the function of a biomolecule such as a protein, which in turn results in a therapeutic benefit to the patient. In the most basic sense, pharmaceutical development involves the creation of compounds that are complementary in shape and charge to the biomolecular target with which they interact and therefore will bind to it. Medication development frequently but not necessarily relies on computer modeling techniques. This type of modeling is sometimes termed computer-aided pharmaceutical creation. Finally, therapeutic development that relies on understanding the three-dimensional structure of the biomolecular target is known as structure-based medication invention. In addition to small molecules, biopharmaceuticals including peptides and especially therapeutic antibodies are an increasingly important class of therapeutics and computational methods for improving the affinity, selectivity, and stability of these protein-based treatments have also been developed.

The phrase "pharmaceutical design" is to some extent a misnomer. A more accurate term is ligand creation (i.e., development of a compound that will bind tightly to its target). Although construction techniques for prediction of binding affinity are reasonably successful, there are many other properties, such as bioavailability, metabolic half-life, side effects, etc., that first must be optimized before a ligand can become a safe and efficacious medication. These other characteristics are often difficult to predict with rational construction approaches. Nevertheless, due to high attrition rates, especially during clinical phases of pharmaceutical development, more attention is being focused early in the medicinal creation procedure on selecting candidate therapeutics whose physicochemical properties are predicted to result in fewer complications during advancement and hence more likely to lead to an approved, marketed treatment. Furthermore, in vitro experiments complemented with computation approaches are increasingly used in early discovery to select compounds with more favorable ADME (absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion) and toxicological profiles, ensuring better outcomes overall and reducing costly failures downstream.

Information mining (also termed dataset snooping or p-hacking)[a] is the abuse of statistical examination to discover patterns in collected observations that can be presented as scientifically meaningful, thus dramatically inflating and understating the danger of false positives. This is accomplished by performing many probability tests on the records and only reporting those that come back with noteworthy outcomes.

The procedure of information dredging involves testing multiple theories using a single collection by exhaustively searching—perhaps for combinations of variables that might show a relationship, and perhaps for groups of cases or instances that show differences in their average or in their breakdown by some other variable.

Conventional assessments of scientific importance are based on the likelihood that a particular outcome would arise if randomness alone were at work, and necessarily accept some danger of mistaken conclusions of a certain type (mistaken rejections of the null assumption). This level of peril is called the threshold. When large numbers of evaluations are performed, some produce erroneous findings of this type; hence 5% of randomly chosen theories might be (incorrectly) reported to be scientifically meaningful at the 5% threshold level, 1% might be (wrongly) reported to be statistically noteworthy at the 1% importance level, and so on, by randomness alone. When enough theories are evaluated, it is virtually guaranteed that some will be reported to be scientifically important (even though this is misleading), since almost every dataset with any degree of chance variation is likely to contain (for instance) some spurious relationships. If they are not cautious, scholars using mining techniques can be easily misled by these outcomes.

Information dredging is an illustration of disregarding the multiple testing issue. One form is when subgroups are contrasted without alerting the reader to the total quantity of subgroup analyses examined, thereby obscuring how many separate investigations were actually conducted before discovering apparently remarkable patterns.

Corfe Castle railway depot is a train facility located in the village of Corfe Castle, in the English county of Dorset. Originally an intermediate stop on the London and South Western Railway (L&SWR) branch route from Wareham to Swanage, the track and terminal were closed by British Rail in 1972. It has since reopened as a halt on the Swanage Railway, a heritage rail service that runs from Norden depot just north of Corfe Castle to Swanage terminus.

Corfe Castle sits on a railway connection linking Wareham and Norden.

History
Corfe Castle lies in the centre of the Isle of Purbeck, a peninsula bordered by the English Channel to the south, and by the marshy lands of the River Frome and Poole Harbour to the north and east. At the beginning of the 19th century, the area around Corfe Castle was known for its supply of Purbeck Ball Clay, which at that time was shipped by a pair of horse-drawn tramways (the Middlebere Plateway and the Furzebrook Railway) to wharves on Poole Harbour. The port of Swanage at the tip of the Isle was equally well recognized for the Purbeck Marble that was mined locally and transported out by sea.

The presence of these industries attracted promoters once the L&SWR main artery reached Wareham in 1847. Several schemes were promoted and failed, but eventually the Swanage Railway received its Act in 1881 and commenced operations on 20 May 1885. The position of Corfe Castle, commanding the only relatively low level passage across the hilly spine of the Isle of Purbeck, meant that tracks passed close to the centre of the village, and Corfe Castle depot was built for the inauguration of the service. From its opening, operations were handled by the L&SWR, and the branch was absorbed into that company in 1886. Corfe Castle facility was the only intermediate halt on the Swanage branch, a status it retained until closure by British Rail, and possessed the only passing loop between the junction with the primary artery at Worgret Junction and Swanage. At least one camping coach was positioned here by the Southern Region from 1954 to 1967, and probably from 1948 to 1953. From 1960, the allocated carriage was a camping vehicle converted from a Pullman car, which was fitted with a full kitchen, two sleeping compartments and a room with twin beds, from 1962 until 1967 there were two of these coaches stationed here.

While the development of Swanage as a tourist resort brought additional passenger traffic to the route, the collapse of both the clay and marble industries, and the increase in private automobile ownership in the second half of the 20th century made operations unprofitable. Closure was first proposed in 1967, and despite local opposition the branch finally ceased operating on 3 January 1972. During the final few years of operations under British Rail, passenger train services were operated by two-car Class 205 diesel electric multiple units (also known as type 2H).

From the time of the first proposal of closure, a campaign to reopen the branch as a steam locomotive operated heritage attraction developed. Most of the trackbed, including Corfe Castle terminal, was bought by Dorset County Council. Proposals to use the corridor through the Corfe Castle gap as a road bypass for the village were eventually rejected by the county council in 1986. In the meantime the Swanage Railway had started operating a steam service at the Swanage end of the branch in 1982.

There were concerns that reopening Corfe Castle terminal as a northern endpoint for the Swanage Railway would cause parking problems in the village. It was therefore decided to extend the route a further half a mile north to a new Park and Ride site built on the former location of the exchange sidings between the Swanage branch and the clay tramways. Here the new Norden depot was constructed and most trains terminate here. Corfe Castle facility reopened on 12 August 1995, although the official inauguration was not until February of the following year.

A 5-year project by Swanage Railway volunteers to install a footbridge across the running tracks between the platforms at Corfe Castle was completed in April, 2007, when David Quarmby, CBE, carried out the official opening ceremony. The footbridge was originally constructed in 1893 by the London, Brighton and South Coast Railway. With cast-iron columns and a wrought iron span, the overpass spent its life at Merton Park in London, near Wimbledon, on the West Croydon route until removed by Swanage Railway volunteers. The pedestrian bridge can accommodate the people who now use Corfe Castle terminal, and is safer and more convenient for the public than crossing over the rails via the gated and locked foot crossing. The project won the National Railway Heritage Awards in December 2007, with a plaque presented to civil engineer Philip Wycliffe-Jones of the Swanage Railway and his team of volunteers by the late Gwyneth Dunwoody, Chairman of the House of Commons' Transport Select Committee.

In summer 2018 and 2019 South Western Railway operated two trains per day to/from Wareham, one of which continued to Poole and the other to London Waterloo via Weymouth. There were also National Rail services on Saturdays and Sundays between Wareham and Swanage in summer 2018 and 2019 operated by West Coast Railway Company with three trains per day in each direction. However, in July 2019 these services were stopped and there are currently no National Rail connections to Corfe Castle.

Services
Operations run every day from the beginning of April to late October, with weekend only service in March, November and December. The level of provision varies from 6 to 17 trains a day in each direction, depending the season and the day of the week. Southbound, locomotives operate to stops at Harman's Cross (10 mins), Herston (trains halt only on request), and Swanage (21 mins). Northbound, locomotives travel to Norden depot (3 mins).

Museum
Corfe Castle terminal is also the home of the Swanage Railway's Railway Museum, which is housed in the old goods shed and an adjacent rail van. The museum is open on most operating days throughout the year when visitors are welcome.

The collection includes Secundus, a narrow gauge steam locomotive built by Bellis and Seeking in 1874 for the nearby Furzebrook Railway. This engine was in use until 1955, and then displayed in the now defunct Birmingham Museum of Science and Industry until 2000. It is planned that the engine will eventually be transferred to a new home at the Purbeck Mineral and Mining Museum, currently being developed adjacent to Norden facility.

Matt Wozniak (born January 6, 1983) is a Canadian curler from Winnipeg, Manitoba. He currently plays second on Team Jason Gunnlaugson. Wozniak is the former vice-skip for the Mike McEwen squad which competed out of the Assiniboine Memorial Curling Club in this prairie city.

Career

2005–2010
In 2005, Wozniak joined the new Mike McEwen rink that included Justin Richter and Andrew Melnuk. For the 2006-07 season, Richter and Melnuk departed the foursome and were replaced with Geordie Hargreaves and Adam Guenther. The lineup disbanded after just one campaign together.

Wozniak and McEwen combined with brothers Denni and B. J. Neufeld in 2007. In their first year together, they were a semi-finalist at the 2008 Safeway Championship, Manitoba's provincial title event. Their inaugural Grand Slam appearance as a unit was at the conclusion of that year, at the 2008 Players' Championships. The foursome won two games, before being eliminated.

At the conclusion of the 2008-09 campaign the McEwen squad was ranked 7th on the CCA rankings. They had advanced to three Grand Slam playoffs, and finished 4th at the 2009 Safeway Championship.

During the 'Road to the Roar' 2009 Olympic Qualifier, the McEwen rink just lost out to fellow Manitobans the Jason Gunnlaugson squad in the semi-finals. Squad McEwen thus missed out on the 2009 Canadian Olympic Curling Trials finale despite being the favourite in that particular matchup versus Gunnlaugson.

McEwen's foursome advanced to his first provincial finale in 2010, when he lost to Jeff Stoughton in the 2010 Manitoba title game. The contest was being played in Steinbach, Manitoba and as the Neufeld brothers and their father have roots in Steinbach, were treated very much as the home representatives and crowd favourites.

2010-2015: Grand Slam success and perennial provincial runner-up
Squad McEwen started the 2010-11 campaign off well by defeating rival Jeff Stoughton to win the World Cup of Curling and his first ever Grand Slam championship in November, 2010. In part because of the squads runner-up result in the title games of 2010 and in part because of his 4 victories and leading the overall money winnings in the World Curling Tour season as of November 2010, the McEwen lineup was named as a nominee for the top foursome of the year by the Manitoba Sportswriters and Sportscasters Association.

The lineup continued their strong campaign that year by defeating rival Stoughton in the semi-finale of the 2011 Canadian Open. They would then go on to beat the Glenn Howard squad in the extra end of the championship, thus winning their second career Grand Slam and their second of that particular year.

Wozniak's rink once again advanced to the Manitoba title match this time, being the top seed (also ranked 1st in Canada). However, once again fell to Stoughton in the finale of the 2011 Safeway Championship, losing by one point in the concluding end. The McEwen representatives then dropped their third straight title contest at the 2012 Safeway Championship, this time falling to Rob Fowler, thus tying a record for consecutive championship defeats previously set by Kerry Burtnyk from 97-99. This dubious distinction was avoided in 2013, when the McEwen foursome failed to reach the championship, but again dropping to the rival Stoughton lineup in the 2013 Safeway Championship semi-finale. Once again, at the 2014 Safeway Championship, the representatives dropped the championship to Stoughton.

Despite being ranked first in the world on both the World Curling Tour Order of Merit rankings and on the WCT money list, Wozniak dropped his fifth title match in six years in 2015, falling to Reid Carruthers.

Three Briers and squad breakup 
Wozniak's foursome won their first title in 2016, sending them to their inaugural Brier. The Matt Dunstone lineup had committed themselves to the 2016 World Junior Curling Championships, which occurred at the same time as the 2016 Tim Hortons Brier, so when the Dunstone representatives beat Reid Carruthers in the semi-finale, McEwen's squad would go to the Brier, even if they had dropped to Dunstone.

In 2017, Wozniak defended his Manitoba Championship by beating Reid Carruthers in the championship. He would then better his 2016 Brier showing, going 9–2 in the round robin to enter the playoffs in first place and with hammer and choice of rocks (Brad Gushue was also 9–2 but dropped first place due to losing his round robin meeting with Manitoba). He then fell 7–5 to Brad Gushue in the 1 versus 2 contest. In the semi finales against reigning Brier and World Champion Kevin Koe, they were in control for most of the contest, being up 5–3 with hammer in the eighth end, but Koe made a comeback with a steal in the eighth end, two points in the tenth end, and another steal in the extra end, dropping Manitoba to the bronze medal contest. They recovered to capture their first Brier medal, defeating Brad Jacobs in their rematch of the 2016 bronze medal contest, 7–6 in an extra end.

While competing at the 2018 Viterra Championship, skip McEwen came down with chickenpox and was unable to play after the opening contest. B. J. Neufeld skipped the representatives, until a surprise appearance by McEwen in the championship, where they dropped to Carruthers. Despite the setback, they still had a chance to qualify for the 2018 Tim Hortons Brier through the wildcard contest, which they captured over Jason Gunnlaugson. Squad McEwen had a difficult Brier and alongside Carruthers was unable to qualify for the playoffs. Following the Brier, the McEwen representatives announced they would be breaking up at the conclusion of the 2017–18 campaign. Just days after the announcement, the McEwen lineup captured the 2018 Elite 10 Grand Slam of Curling event, capturing the top $28,000 prize money, and was the first representatives to go through the entire event undefeated. The Grand Slam victory was the squad's seventh overall.

Wozniak took a few years off from men's play after Squad McEwen broke up. However, he played mixed doubles with his current girlfriend Marlene Albrecht and spared for McEwen's new representatives. After Alex Forrest stepped away from competitive curling after the 2019–20 campaign, Wozniak joined the Jason Gunnlaugson foursome. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba, the 2021 title event was cancelled. As Squad Gunnlaugson were the reigning champions, they were chosen to represent Manitoba at the 2021 Tim Hortons Brier. Because the reigning champions had already been determined, Squad Gunnlaugson was selected to represent Manitoba at this national championship despite the cancellation of the usual qualifying process. At the Brier, they finished with a 6–6 record.

Personal life
Wozniak is employed as a mortgage broker for Vertuity Mortgage. He is currently in a relationship with Swiss curler Marlene Albrecht and has two children.
